The weekly 'dots' duplicate the existing 'На этой неделе: 3 из 5' bar (TodayCard.tsx:116-122) and the streak. The persona need (show friends) is already met by printed rank certificates; a lower-risk alternative if wanted is a 'save image' button on the existing certificate. There is no evidence in the proposal that sharing improves learning or return.

#### ONB-S12 · drop · effort L · impact 4 — NEW: 'Мастерская робота' - progress as a growing robot (capped at 12 parts) with XP kept for older kids

- **Addresses:** (new idea)
- **Proposal:** For junior (and as an option for all) replace the XP/level bar on home with a small Robot Workshop: the mascot robot on the hero gains a part (antenna, gear, arm, scarf, hat...) when a finished round, a day or an effort behaviour happens: 'tried another way', 'opened a hint and then solved it', 'explained why' (the owner's three rules), never for speed or streak length. 12 parts in total, then the robot is 'готов' and a new colour/hat set can be chosen (cosmetic, free). XP and levels remain on a secondary 'Мои успехи' screen for Dilnoza. Robot states for micro-feedback: ready, thinking (hand on chin while a hint is open), happy (solved), cheering (round end). Robot animations are 1-2 seconds and never block the next action. The same character appears in welcome step 1, RobotTip, RestStop and the hero, giving the product a consistent face.
- **UI spec:** Robot SVG 72 px on home hero (right side of greeting row), 12 slots; a new part flies in 600 ms with a soft 'click' sound and a one-line caption ('Новая деталь: антенна!'). Workshop sheet: robot 160 px, 12 slots with earned (colour) and unearned (outline) parts and a caption of HOW each was earned in plain words ('За другой способ'). Reduced motion: part appears with a 150 ms fade only. No numbers on the junior view except 'N из 12'.
- **Files:** src/components/Logo.tsx, src/components/visuals/RobotMascot.tsx (new), src/components/home/HomeDashboard.tsx, src/components/progress/XpToast.tsx, src/lib/xp.ts, src/lib/awards.ts
- **Inspired by:** Khan Academy Kids (character that reacts, accumulating sparkles toward a payoff), Lingokids stickers/album, Mathseeds hatching creature; Mueller and Dweck (praise process, not ability); Deci et al. 1999 (informational rewards).
- **Guardrails:** Rewards are not random (no mystery boxes), not purchasable, not time-limited and never lost; the collection has an end (12). Parts are given for process behaviours, not speed or time on app. The robot never looks disappointed when the child stops or errs. No 'complete your robot today' reminders. Cosmetics unlocked by effort only.
- **Test plan:** Unit: part-award rules (once per behaviour per day, cap 12). E2E: seeded events produce expected parts; reaching 12 shows the 'ready' state once. Check that no award is triggered by time-on-app or first-try speed. Usability with 5 children 6-8: can they say how to get a new part (comprehension) and do they ask for it before the task (over-justification check: compare willingness to do a no-reward Lab task afterwards).
- **Review:** feasibility hard, age fit False, manipulation risk high. A 12-part collect-them robot is a new reward currency on top of XP, levels, quest stars, streak, awards and crowns, i.e. six systems already. The triggers are the problem: 'explained why' and 'tried another way' are self-reported checkboxes in AfterSolve.tsx:9-14, so a child can earn parts by tapping them, which trains ticking boxes rather than thinking. 'Opened a hint then solved it' rewards using hints, so a child learns to open one to get a part (and xp.ts already penalises no-hint, so the economy is contradictory). A finite collectible set with a visible completion state is a completionist mechanic, whatever the guardrails say. Effort is L (new mascot SVG, slots, awards, XP toast rework) and it does not address first run, home layout or wayfinding. Existing mascot SVG and the robot in the welcome already give a consistent face at no cost.

#### ONB-S13 · modify · effort S · impact 2 — NEW: Parent-side 'Put it on the phone screen' card and persistent storage, so the child's path back is one tap

- **Addresses:** (new idea)
- **Proposal:** Aziz returns by tapping an icon, not by typing a URL. After the first completed day (not on first launch, not in a task) and permanently in /parent, show a parent-addressed card: 'Поставьте Davlatjon на экран телефона' with a big app icon, a single 'Установить' button wired to beforeinstallprompt (Android Chrome), and for iOS Safari a 3-picture guide (Share, Add to Home Screen, Add). The card is dismissible and then lives only in /parent. At install time and after the first reward call navigator.storage.persist() and show in /parent a line 'Прогресс хранится на этом телефоне' with an optional 'Сохранить копию' export (short code or file) so a cleared browser does not erase certificates and crowns. Fix manifest.ts copy ('от 7 лет' vs the 6-12 product) and add the Uzbek manifest strings.
- **Revised after review:** Do the small things: fix manifest description to 6-12; call navigator.storage.persist() once after the first solved task (silent); on /parent only, add a parent-addressed 'Поставьте Davlatjon на экран телефона' card using beforeinstallprompt on Android Chrome and a 3-step picture guide for iOS, with 'Не сейчас' of equal size and 14 days of silence. Do not add a new backup flow (use the existing progress file) and no child-side prompt. Skip Uzbek manifest.
- **UI spec:** Card in /parent top: icon 64 px, title text-lg, one primary button h-14, secondary 'Не сейчас' h-14 (same size), 3-step iOS illustration with 48 px numbered circles. On the child's side nothing appears except the installed icon. States: installed (hide card), unsupported browser (show only the iOS guide or nothing), prompt dismissed (do not re-prompt for 14 days).
- **Files:** src/app/manifest.ts, src/components/ServiceWorker.tsx, src/components/parent/ (parent page cards), public/sw.js, src/lib/store.ts
- **Inspired by:** web.dev install best practices; Khan Academy Kids parent area; local-context research (cheap Android, shared phones, risk of cleared storage).
- **Guardrails:** Never prompt the child; no repeated nagging (one dismiss = 14 days of silence). Do not promise data safety (persist() may be denied). No account is required for the backup. Do not request notification permission.
- **Test plan:** Playwright: no beforeinstallprompt UI on first launch or inside tasks; card appears in /parent after day 1; dismissed state persists. Unit: persist() called once after first reward and failure is silent. Manifest validates (Lighthouse PWA) and the description says 6-12.
- **Review:** feasibility easy, age fit True, manipulation risk none. The insight is good: a home-screen icon is the best return path for Aziz on a shared Android phone, and the manifest copy is wrong ('для детей от 7 лет', manifest.ts:8, versus a 6-12 product). The product has no install handling at all (grep finds no beforeinstallprompt or storage.persist). But a card visible only in /parent behind a PIN is rarely seen; and showing it on the child's home would put an adult card in the child's path, against S5. 'Uzbek manifest strings' is not possible per user: a manifest has one lang. The backup duplicates what exists (SettingsPanel.tsx:30-46 already saves and loads a progress file, and Google/Telegram sync is in progress). Persist is silent and cheap.

## Math task experience

The task experience is a strong foundation. Soft wording, a thoughtful hint ladder, tactile tools (robot, scales, Hanoi, number machine) and full RU/UZ narration are all there. What is missing is the emotional layer around it, and a few layout and copy problems. After a correct answer the reward is half-hidden: the feedback is clipped by the fixed bottom bar and the XP toast covers "Дальше". The end of the day is a reading-heavy questionnaire rather than a celebration. Russian copy addresses the child in the masculine ("объяснил", "справился", "поработал"), against the owner's own principle (the test profile is "Анна"). About 60% of tasks (99 of about 165) are "type a number and press Проверить", and the generic retry text for them is meaningless. On a 6.3" phone the fixed header and bottom bar take about 21% of the screen, so the robot flag and the controls cannot be seen together. For Aziz the main risk is reading load plus a small, unobtrusive "Прочитать" button. For Dilnoza it is the lack of visible in-day progress and a payoff at the end.

**Keep (strengths):**

- Soft-feedback wording is consistent and well written: no 'wrong', rotating phrases like «Давай проверим твою идею!», «Пока не сходится», and a hint to open a hint appears only after 2+ misses (src/lib/feedback.ts:28-75). Keep.
- The tools give specific, causal feedback, not just 'try again': robot says «Ой! На шаге 1 робот вышел бы за край поля… можно нажимать «Шаг»» and highlights the offending command in red (c-robot-after-wrong-vp.png); Hanoi says «Большое кольцо нельзя класть на маленькое!»; scales explain why the weighing teaches nothing (ScalesPuzzle.tsx:179-185). This is the best part of the product.
- The hint ladder: 5 steps that open one by one, a visual dot counter, a 15-second pause with a countdown ring and the label «Подумай с этой подсказкой…», and the full answer is never shown (HintLadder.tsx). Matches the owner's principle and is well explained to the child.
- Tools are tactile and visual: 3D-pressed buttons, big arrow pad (48 px), animated robot run with a trail, visible scales and pegs, a 'My records' grid in Hanoi, a 'program: N commands / short form 3↑ 4→' readout. Real manipulation instead of typing.
- Recorded narration exists for all 165 tasks in both RU and UZ (voice-clips.json: 165 task entries per language, mp3 files present), the button is hidden if sound is off, and there is no browser speech.
- Recovery is cheap: input is saved (saveTaskInput), unlimited re-checks, «Назад», «Стереть/Очистить/На старт/Как было», a ✓ badge on solved tasks and on the title, solved state survives navigation. Day intro says solving everything is not required.
- «А ещё подумай» and process marks (explained / another way / liked / hard but did it) and the day-end 'favourite / hardest task' reflect a thinking-habits pedagogy, not just correct answers (AfterSolve.tsx, DayFinish.tsx).
- Technically clean on the day page: 0 unnamed interactive elements, no horizontal overflow, text is mostly 18-20 px with relaxed line height, ratio of page to viewport is only 1.8-1.9 so tasks are short scrolls (audit-metrics.json).

### Findings

#### TASK-1 · major · confirmed — The moment after a correct answer is muffled: feedback is clipped, the XP toast covers «Дальше», nothing guides the next step

- **Who:** AZIZ, DILNOZA
- **Problem:** The success message appears under the check button at y≈700-780 of an 839 px viewport, and the fixed bottom bar (starts at about y=770) cuts its second line. The «+15 XP ⭐» toast is positioned fixed right-4 bottom-4, which is exactly where the primary «Дальше →» button sits, so for ~1.8 s (the best moment to press) the next step is hidden. The page does not scroll to the feedback or to the 'А ещё подумай' block, which is entirely below the fold. «Дальше» is the same indigo primary button before and after solving, so solving does not change what the screen invites the child to do. The celebration is a static 🎉 emoji and a 'pop' animation, with no sound cue beyond a voice clip and no visual reward beyond the small ✓.
- **Evidence:** Playwright screenshot audit-agents/task/a-t1-right-0.5s.png: toast overlaps «Дальше →»; success card cut mid-sentence ('Сможешь объяснить, почему это'); audit-agents/task/a-t1-right-full.png: 'А ещё подумай' and the 4 marks are below the nav bar; src/components/progress/XpToast.tsx:38 (fixed right-4 bottom-4 z-50) vs src/components/session/DaySession.tsx:82-97 (fixed bottom nav z-20); src/components/answers/Feedback.tsx:309-336 has no scrollIntoView; src/components/session/DaySession.tsx:93 «Дальше» is unchanged after a solve
- **Principle:** Immediate, visible reinforcement and one clear next action (Hick's law, Fogg's 'celebrate right after the behaviour'); do not let transient UI cover the primary control. Duolingo/Khan Kids give a full-width 'Continue' bar that turns green with the result.
- **Impact:** The child gets a weaker emotional payoff from every correct answer, Aziz may miss the praise text (he reads slowly), and the 'explain it' follow-up that the owner cares about is rarely seen.
- **Skeptic:** Reproduced on a Pixel 7 at age 7. After a correct answer the XP toast box (x274 y779, 122x44) covers the «Дальше» button (x284 y783, 113x44) almost exactly. The toast is gone by about 2.6 s. scrollY stays 0, so no auto-scroll happens. The «Yana o'ylab ko'r» / «А ещё подумай» block starts at y≈857, below the 839 px viewport, with the nav bar's top at y=770. «Дальше» keeps the same indigo primary class after the solve. The success card is cut mid-sentence by the nav in a-t1-right-0.5s.png. No scrollIntoView exists anywhere in src/components. The same cut-off hits the retry card: in a-t1-wrong.png its bottom edge is under the nav bar.

#### TASK-2 · major · confirmed — Russian copy addresses the child in the masculine, against the owner's gender-neutral principle

- **Who:** AZIZ, DILNOZA, PARENT
- **Problem:** Several high-frequency strings use masculine past-tense forms or adjectives: «Я объяснил решение», «Я нашёл другой способ», «Было трудно, но я справился» (every solved task); «Ты хорошо поработал!», «объяснил решение», «нашёл другой способ», «не сдался в трудной» (every day finish); «Застрял?» (every hint box); «Ты нашёл все пути/способы/числа/суммы» (robot, partition, wall lab, magic triangle, chess). The test profile is «Анна», and the greeting shows it, so a girl is told «я справился». Uzbek avoids this naturally, so only RU is affected.
- **Evidence:** src/components/task/AfterSolve.tsx:9-12; src/components/session/DayFinish.tsx:50,60,61,64; src/components/task/HintLadder.tsx:59; src/components/robot/RobotPuzzle.tsx:233; src/components/answers/GridPuzzles.tsx:279; WallLab.tsx:113; MagicTrianglePuzzle.tsx:236; src/components/chess/ChessExercises.tsx:709; audit-agents/task/a-t1-right-full.png (marks list) and f-finish-solved-full.png (stats labels)
- **Principle:** Inclusive language and identity safety; the owner's explicit rule. Self-efficacy messages work best when the child can recognise herself in them.
- **Impact:** Girls (about half of the audience) see a statement that is not about them in the most emotional spots (finish, 'I managed'); parents notice.
- **Skeptic:** All cited strings exist and are shown in ru to every child. AfterSolve.tsx:9-12 «Я объяснил решение / Я нашёл другой способ / Было трудно, но я справился». DayFinish.tsx:50,60,61,64 «Ты хорошо поработал», «объяснил решение», «нашёл другой способ», «не сдался в трудной». HintLadder.tsx:59 «Застрял? … подумать сам». RobotPuzzle.tsx:233, GridPuzzles.tsx:279, ChessExercises.tsx:709 and the two match-strings in the wall-lab and magic-triangle components say «Ты нашёл…». The Uzbek versions are neutral. The finish page screenshot f-finish-solved-full.png shows the masculine stat labels. This breaks the owner's stated principle.

#### TASK-3 · minor · partly — 60% of the tasks are the same «type a number, press Проверить» pattern; the rich tools appear about once per day

- **Who:** DILNOZA, AZIZ
- **Problem:** Counting answer kinds across weeks 1-3 gives 99 'fields' (mostly number inputs), 17 'choice', 15 'assign', 6 'robot', and 19 other kinds with 1-2 tasks each (scales 2, performer 2, hanoi 1, nim 1, cipher 1, …) — out of about 165 tasks. A 7-year-old and a 10-year-old will repeat the same keyboard interaction for most of the day, with the pictured/tool tasks as islands (one per day: day-5 task in w2d2, w2d3, w3d4, w3d6 …). There is no drag/tap on the problem's own picture for a typical word problem (stickers, coins, sequences) and no number pad made for the child.
- **Evidence:** grep of kind: counts over src/content/week*/day?.ts (fields 99, choice 17, assign 15, robot 6, scales 2, performer 2, others 1 each); src/components/answers/FieldsAnswer.tsx:70-84 (plain numeric input, 28 rem wide, typed by system keyboard); day-by-day: w2d2t5 performer, w2d3t5 hanoi, w3d4t5/t8 scales, w3d6t5 cipher, w3d7t4 nim, w2d4t5 crossing are all at positions 4-8
- **Principle:** Variety and 'direct manipulation' keep young learners engaged (Khan Academy Kids, Prodigy, Matific, Toca-style tool-first design); a system keyboard slows 6-8 year olds and hides the problem while open.
- **Impact:** Engagement drops in the second half of a day and across weeks; Aziz types with a full-screen Android keyboard that covers the question and the check button.
- **Skeptic:** The counts are right: fields 99, choice 17, assign 15, robot 6, and about 20 other kinds with 1-2 tasks each, all measured with grep over week*/day?.ts. But the keyboard claim is overstated. The number input uses inputMode="numeric" (a digit pad, not a full keyboard) and is w-28 (112 px), not 28 rem. «fields» also covers time, coord and text inputs, so not all 99 are typed digits. Typing numbers for arithmetic is also legitimate for 6-12 year olds. What stands is the lack of variety and the tool tasks appearing as islands. I could not emulate the Android keyboard height covering the check button.

#### TASK-4 · major · confirmed — The retry message for a plain number answer is generic and meaningless

- **Who:** AZIZ, DILNOZA
- **Problem:** For a single-number field the retry card says «Давай проверим твою идею! 🤔 / Какая часть решения точно верная?» (the emoji is also duplicated — once as the icon and once in the title). There is no 'part of the solution' in 19+19+19. The rotation by attempt number (n % 4) means the same child gets 'Не сдавайся!' or 'Интересная попытка!' regardless of what happened. The text never connects to the task, never says what to look at (e.g. 'проверь, сколько раз повторяется 19'), and gives a 7-year-old a long sentence he must read. Only after 2 misses does it point to the hint button.
- **Evidence:** audit-agents/task/a-t1-wrong.png; src/lib/feedback.ts:28-75 (RETRY_TITLE/RETRY_SUB are task-agnostic); src/components/answers/FieldsAnswer.tsx:40-50 ('some && fields.length > 1' is the only contextual branch)
- **Principle:** Feedback should be specific and actionable (Hattie & Timperley: 'where to next'); generic encouragement without direction lowers perceived competence. Short and spoken for pre-readers.
- **Impact:** The most common failure state (60% of tasks) feels like a template. The child gets no usable next step, which pushes him toward either guessing or skipping.
- **Skeptic:** Reproduced three wrong tries on w1d1 task 1. The titles come out as «Давай проверим твою идею! 🤔», then «Пока не сходится.», then «Интересная попытка!», with no link to the task. The first one pairs with «Какая часть решения точно верная?» for 19+19+19, and the 🤔 is doubled (icon plus title) in a-t1-wrong.png. feedback.ts:28-75 is task-agnostic and rotates by n%4. The hint pointer is added only when n>=2 (retrySub). The only contextual branch is the multi-field «Часть ответа сходится ✓». Note the hint text itself is specific («Сколько раз в нём повторяется число 19?»), so the content exists but is not surfaced from the retry card.

#### TASK-5 · minor · partly — On a phone the fixed header + bottom bar leave about 79% of the screen, and tool tasks cannot show goal and controls at once

- **Who:** AZIZ
- **Problem:** The sticky header with the task strip is about 112 CSS px tall and the fixed bottom nav is about 68 px, i.e. 180 of 839 px (21%) are permanently taken. In the robot task, the board (4 rows, flag in the top row) and the arrow pad are about 330 px apart: when the arrows are on screen, the flag row is scrolled out of view, and after a successful run the robot sits at the flag, which is also off screen (only the blue trail is visible). The same stacking (board, then program, then controls, then feedback) applies to Hanoi, scales and the number machine, where the interactive area is cut by the bar in full-page shots and the feedback appears below the controls.
- **Evidence:** audit-agents/task/c-robot-arrows-vp.png and c-robot-solved-vp.png (top row with flag not visible; trail only); audit-agents/task/b-t5-full.png; src/components/session/DaySession.tsx:51 (sticky header) and :82-97 (fixed nav); src/components/robot/RobotPuzzle.tsx:352-433 (board then program then arrows in one column)
- **Principle:** Keep the goal and the controls in one viewport (Fitts/proximity; 'no hidden state'); reduce persistent chrome on small screens.
- **Impact:** Aziz loses the thread of 'where is my robot and where do I need to go'; he re-scrolls after every command, which breaks the 10-minute attention budget.
- **Skeptic:** The chrome numbers hold: the header is 113 px and the nav 69 px, 182 of 839 px (21.7%). But the central claim that goal and controls cannot be seen together is refuted. In the robot task the document y of the board SVG is 612-842 and the arrow pad is at 964-1066, so the span is about 450 px. At scrollY=500 (qa-task/robot-500.png) the flag, the robot, the walls, the program row and all four arrows are on screen at once, with Запустить below. The earlier screenshots just caught an unlucky scroll position. The real problem is that nothing scrolls the child to that sweet spot. After the first arrow tap or a solve, the feedback sits below the controls and out of view.

#### TASK-6 · major · confirmed — Reading load for pre-readers: the narration button is small and optional, and only the task statement is narrated

- **Who:** AZIZ
- **Problem:** A task card has a title, a chip row (section, level, 'Задача N из M') and statements of up to ~70 words (Hanoi, robot, scales + a note). The «Прочитать» button is the smallest control in the card (122x36 px, text-sm, pale brand-soft background, wraps to a second line in Uzbek) and nothing plays automatically for a child whose age is 6-7. Hints (5 per task, text only), the «А ещё подумай» questions, the feedback sub-lines, and the finish page have no audio at all; only a short praise/retry clip is played. Task intros, the day intro and the 8-title pickers at day finish are also text-only.
- **Evidence:** audit-agents/task/a-t1-initial.png and tile rich-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg (button at far right of chip row); audit-agents/task/richuz-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg (button wraps under the chips); src/components/task/TaskView.tsx:57 is the only ListenButton in the task flow; src/components/ListenButton.tsx min-h-9 text-sm; src/components/task/HintLadder.tsx:228-237 no audio per hint
- **Principle:** Dual coding and low reading load for emergent readers (Sesame/Khan Kids read everything aloud and make the speaker the largest icon); target size and prominence should match the user.
- **Impact:** Aziz either does not find the voice or can only be helped on the statement; he is left alone with a hint he cannot read, which is exactly when he needs support.
- **Skeptic:** ListenButton is rendered only at TaskView.tsx:57 inside the task flow. Measured 122x36 px, text-sm, pale brand-soft. In Uzbek («Oʻqib berish») it wraps to its own row under the chips (richuz-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg). Hints (HintLadder), follow-ups, feedback and the finish page have no ListenButton. VOICE_CLIPS has a task clip only. Nothing in task, answers or session components calls playClip, so nothing plays automatically, even at age 7. The claim about a «praise/retry clip» is unverified, since I found no playClip call in Feedback.tsx.

#### TASK-7 · major · partly — The end of the day is a questionnaire, not a celebration, and the 'next day' step is hidden

- **Who:** AZIZ, DILNOZA
- **Problem:** The finish page shows a flag emoji and 4 counters, then 3 reflective questions where two of them ask the child to pick from 8 chips with task titles to read, plus a 4-mood row with 12 px labels. There are no XP, level, streak, or star summary, no animation, and no 'tomorrow' hook. Pressing «Завершить день ✓» calls router.push('/'), so the «Следующий день →» button (shown only when `nextDayHref && done`) cannot be seen the first time; the only celebration is a '+20 XP' toast on the home page. The 🏁 chip can open the page at 0/8 solved and it still says «Ты хорошо поработал!» over a row of zeros, with 'Завершить день' available.
- **Evidence:** audit-agents/task/f-finish-solved-full.png and f-after-finish-vp.png (+20 XP toast over home); src/components/session/DayFinish.tsx:36-39,47-67,124-128,130; e-finish text dump: '0 из 8 задач решено … Ты хорошо поработал!' with 'Завершить день ✓'; src/lib/xp.ts:13-14 (XP.day 20) is not shown on the finish page
- **Principle:** Peak-end rule: the end of a session defines how it is remembered; give a visible reward, a progress summary, and one clear next step. Reflection tasks should be short and pictorial for a 7-year-old.
- **Impact:** A child who has just worked for 20-30 minutes gets homework-like questions instead of pride; no reason to come back tomorrow.
- **Skeptic:** Mostly right. The finish page has 4 counters and three reflective questions, with two 8-chip pickers of task titles and a 12 px mood row (f-finish-solved-full.png). It shows no XP, level or tomorrow hook, though XP.day=20 exists. «Ты хорошо поработал» is static text, so it shows even with 0 solved. finish() does router.push("/"), and the «Следующий день →» link needs nextDayHref && done, but done is false until finish() sets completedAt. So the next-day button is never seen on the first finish. Overstated: «no animation» is wrong, since the card uses animate-pop, and the 🏁 and the stats are a mild celebration. I did not verify the XP toast on the home page after finishing.

#### TASK-8 · minor · confirmed — Raw markdown asterisks are shown in two week-3 day intros (both languages)

- **Who:** DILNOZA, PARENT
- **Problem:** DayIntro prints each intro paragraph as plain text, while the task bodies go through RichText. Intros of w3d2 and w3d5 contain «**не бывает**», which is shown literally with the asterisks.
- **Evidence:** audit-tiles/rich-phone-w3d5-t1.jpg ('что чего-то **не бывает**'); src/components/session/DayIntro.tsx:215-219 renders {p} directly; src/content/week3/day5.ts:12, week3/day2.ts and the .uz.ts versions
- **Principle:** Polish and trust: visible markup artefacts signal an unfinished product.
- **Impact:** 4 intro paragraphs (2 days x 2 languages) look broken at the moment the child decides whether to start the day.
- **Skeptic:** DayIntro.tsx:39-40 renders {p} as plain text, so ** is printed. The rich-phone-w3d5-t1.jpg tile shows «**не бывает**» literally. A scan of every intro array finds ** only in week3/day2.ts, day5.ts and their .uz.ts versions (4 files). Corrections to the report: the line cited is 39-40, not 215-219. The day2 example is «**предположи и проверь**», not «не бывает».

#### TASK-9 · minor · confirmed — Disabled «Проверить» is a faded dead button; tapping does nothing and explains nothing

- **Who:** AZIZ
- **Problem:** Until all fields are filled the check button is rendered at 45% opacity with pointer-events: none. A child who taps it gets no response and no hint ('впиши число'). The only cue is the '?' placeholder. Same pattern for choice/assign answers, and for the robot's «Запустить/Шаг» before any commands exist.
- **Evidence:** audit-tiles/rich-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg (pale lavender 'Проверить'); src/components/ui.tsx:32 (disabled:opacity-45 disabled:pointer-events-none); src/components/answers/FieldsAnswer.tsx:107
- **Principle:** Do not make controls that look broken to a child; prefer an enabled button that answers gently («Сначала впиши число 🙂») — error prevention without silence.
- **Impact:** Some children will think the app is frozen and call a parent.
- **Skeptic:** Measured: the Проверить button isDisabled, opacity 0.45, pointer-events none (ui.tsx:32, FieldsAnswer.tsx:107 disabled={!allFilled}). It looks faded and a tap does nothing. The «?» placeholder is the only cue. It is a UX smell, not a bug, and the claim that children will think the app is frozen is speculative.

#### TASK-10 · minor · confirmed — Hint area sits at the very bottom, and the XP economy quietly discourages hints

- **Who:** AZIZ, DILNOZA
- **Problem:** The ladder is the last block of the page (after AfterSolve), around y≈1365 on a 1500 px task page, so a stuck child has to scroll past the answer area and there is no pointer to it from the failed-answer card except text. The dot counter is 10 px, and the step label is a 12 px uppercase string. The XP rule gives +5 'clean' bonus only when no hints were opened, so the toast reads «+15 XP» without hints and «+10 XP» with them, which contradicts the on-screen message that hints are normal.
- **Evidence:** audit-agents/task/e-hint1-cooldown-vp.png; src/components/task/HintLadder.tsx:212-214,230; src/lib/xp.ts:12-13 and :34 (XP.taskClean applies only if !t.hints); a-t1-right-0.5s.png shows '+15 XP' (clean solve)
- **Principle:** Do not penalise help-seeking (growth-mindset, Dweck); keep the help close to the problem.
- **Impact:** A shy child may avoid hints to keep the bigger number, and the owner's 'hints are fine' message is undermined by the reward system.
- **Skeptic:** On a single-column phone layout the aside holds AfterSolve then HintLadder, so the hints come after the answer panel (TaskView.tsx:85-89). In e-hint1-cooldown-vp.png the box is reachable only by scrolling. The dots are h-2.5 (10 px). xp.ts:34 gives XP.task+XP.taskClean(5) only when !t.hints, so +15 without hints and +10 with them, which matches what a-t1-right-0.5s.png shows. The hint box itself works well: step label, a specific hint text, and a visible cooldown on «Подсказка 2» for kid7.

#### TASK-11 · minor · confirmed — Several touch targets are below 44 px for a 6-7 year old

- **Who:** AZIZ
- **Problem:** On the day page 11 of 13 targets are below 44 px: back arrow 40x40, print 45x36, each of the 9 task-strip buttons 40x40, Listen 36 px high, «Стереть» and «Очистить» 36 px high (the latter is a ghost button that looks like plain text), Hanoi peg-count chips 40x40, cipher +/- 36x36. Children aged 6-7 have lower motor precision; 48 px or more is advised, with 8 px gaps.
- **Evidence:** audit-metrics.json phone /week/1/day/1: small44=11, smallSamples ['← 40x40','🖨 Распечатать 45x36','🔢 40x40']; audit-agents/task/t2/t4 console output (robot: ⌫ Стереть 109x36, Очистить 109x36; hanoi 1-4 40x40; cipher −/+ 36x36); src/components/ui.tsx:25-27 (sm = min-h-9)
- **Principle:** Touch target size (WCAG 2.5.5 / Material 48 dp), larger for young children.
- **Impact:** Mis-taps on the strip jump the child to another task; 'Очистить' is easy to miss.
- **Skeptic:** My measurement on /week/1/day/1#task-1 lists ← 40x40, 🖨 45x36, 9 strip buttons 40x40, and Прочитать 122x36. That matches audit-metrics.json (small44=11). The robot arrows are 48x48, which is fine, but Стереть and Очистить are 36 px high and Очистить looks like plain text (c-robot-arrows-vp.png). sm is min-h-9 in ui.tsx.

#### TASK-12 · polish · partly — In-day progress is only a strip of section emoji; no counter, no bar, the last chip is clipped

- **Who:** DILNOZA, AZIZ
- **Problem:** The strip uses section emoji as labels, so tasks 1 and 2 look identical (🔢 🔢) and a child cannot see 'where am I' at a glance; the 🏁 chip is cut at the right edge on a 412 px phone. 'Задача N из M' is small muted text, and the day has no solved counter or progress bar, so Dilnoza cannot see 'I have done 5 of 8' without counting ticks.
- **Evidence:** audit-tiles/rich-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg (two identical 🔢, 🏁 clipped); src/components/session/DaySession.tsx:103-163; src/components/session/DayIntro.tsx:246-252 shows 'решено N из M' only on the intro screen
- **Principle:** Visible progress toward a goal (goal-gradient effect); progress needs a legible quantity, not only status marks.
- **Impact:** Weaker sense of momentum and weaker motivation to finish the day.
- **Skeptic:** Real parts: the strip uses section emoji, so tasks 1 and 2 are both 🔢; the 🏁 chip is cut at the right edge on a 412 px viewport. Overstated: it is wrong that «no counter». The strip shows a mint border and a ✓ badge on every solved task (visible in f-finish-solved-full.png and richuz tile), and the nav bar always shows «N / M». Only a «solved X of Y» count is missing during the tasks (DayIntro shows it).

**Missed by the auditor (found by the skeptic):**

- (minor) Retry card is also hidden under the bottom bar, so first-time wrong-answer feedback is not seen without manual scrolling — a-t1-wrong.png: the card begins at y≈1675 of a 2000 px-high render and its bottom edge is covered by the nav bar (top at ≈1835). The sub-line «Какая часть решения…» sits directly on the bar. The Feedback component has no scrollIntoView (grep finds none in src/components). A child at age 7 sees at most the title line, and the XP-toast issue is not involved here.
- (polish) Good, keep: answer and hint state survive a reload, and the hint ladder has a visible cooldown — qa-task/t4.mjs: after a solve and reload, the input value is restored as 57 and Проверить is enabled. e-hint1-cooldown-vp.png: hint 2 shows a timer ring and «Подумай с этой подсказкой…». Positive note for the synthesis so these are not rewritten.

### Solutions

#### TASK-S1 · modify · effort M · impact 5 — Result bar: the correct-answer moment is always visible and 'Дальше' becomes the reward

- **Addresses:** TASK-1
- **Proposal:** Make the moment after a correct answer unmissable and unblocked. (1) Feedback scrolls itself into view above the fixed bottom bar (scroll-margin-bottom of about 96px, smooth unless prefers-reduced-motion). (2) XpToast stops sitting at bottom-right (it currently covers 'Дальше', XpToast.tsx:38). Move it to top-center just under the sticky header (or into the bottom bar's centre slot, where '3 / 8' sits), pointer-events none, 2.4s instead of 1.8s. (3) When the current task flips to solved, the bottom bar changes state: a thin mint top border, 'Дальше →' switches from the indigo 'primary' to the 'success' variant (ui.tsx) with one 600ms pulse, so the screen visibly says 'press this now'. Before solving it stays quiet. (4) A small optional chip '🤔 А ещё подумай ↓' appears in the bar; it scrolls to AfterSolve but is never required. (5) Sound: one neutral soft rising two-note chime (reuse sfx 'collect', volume about 0.4, sfx.ts) played before the existing recorded praise clip; for 'not yet' a soft low two-note 'hm' (new sfx 'hm', never a buzzer). Both respect settings.sound. The robot-style tools (robot, scales, Hanoi) reuse the same Feedback so they inherit this.
- **Revised after review:** Keep (1) scroll-margin plus scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) on the success card and on the first retry only (smooth unless reduced-motion). On pages without a bottom bar (chess) no extra margin. Keep (2) with one change: on DaySession the toast is rendered inside the bottom bar's centre slot (mint pill '⭐ +15', 2.4 s, pointer-events none); elsewhere it stays bottom-right. Mark the bar with data-bottom-nav so XpToast can choose. Drop the top-centre option because it would cover the task chips and title. Keep (3): the bar gets a mint top border and 'Дальше' turns success, with one 600 ms pulse. 'Дальше' keeps the same size and position, and reduced-motion means no pulse. Drop (4) the chip: AfterSolve already renders right below the answer card, so a short scroll shows it. Sound: add one new 'cheer' two-note sfx played only on success, gated on settings.sound AND not boardSounds. Do NOT add an 'hm' sound; the existing retry voice clip is enough. Play the chime first and start the voice clip about 350 ms later. Test plan stays: assert Feedback bottom <= nav top-8 in RU and UZ, toast bbox not intersecting 'Дальше'.
- **UI spec:** Phone 412x839. Bottom bar stays 68px (S13 may trim to 64). Solved state: bar bg white/95 + 3px mint top border; centre slot shows '3 / 8' until solved, then a mint pill '⭐ +15' for 2.4s (toast integrated here on DaySession; XpToast keeps floating at top:calc(env(safe-area-inset-top)+7.5rem) centre on every other page, bottom-right only where no [data-bottom-nav] exists). Feedback card gets scroll-mt/scroll-mb so its whole text (2 lines) is above y=760. 'Дальше →' success variant, min-h-14, pulse = scale 1 -> 1.06 -> 1, once. Chip 'А ещё подумай' 44px high, soft variant, left of Дальше only on screens >=360px; hidden if no followUps. Reduced motion: no pulse, no smooth scroll, toast fades only. Sound: chime 300ms, then cheer() clip with 350ms delay so they do not overlap.
- **Files:** src/components/progress/XpToast.tsx, src/components/session/DaySession.tsx, src/components/answers/Feedback.tsx, src/lib/sfx.ts, src/components/ui.tsx, src/components/task/AfterSolve.tsx
- **Inspired by:** Duolingo's full-width Continue bar that turns green with the result; Khan Academy Kids non-verbal language-neutral cues (but a soft 'hm', not their 'bong'); Fogg: celebrate immediately after the behaviour; Hick's law (one clear next action).
- **Guardrails:** Celebration marks the end of a task, not a loop: no confetti per answer, no streak or loss wording, no countdown on the toast. The pulse and chime happen once and never block input. 'Дальше' is the same size and position before and after solving, so nothing is hidden or auto-advanced (no autoplay of next task). The 'А ещё подумай' chip is optional so reflection is invited, not required. Sound obeys the sound setting; add no audio on retry louder than the success cue.
- **Test plan:** Playwright Pixel 7, day1 task1: type 57, press Проверить. Assert (a) Feedback bounding box bottom <= nav top - 8 for RU and UZ; (b) at t=0.3s and t=1s the XP toast bbox does not intersect the 'Дальше' bbox; (c) 'Дальше' computed background is the success colour after solve and indigo before; (d) with prefers-reduced-motion no animation on bar. Check tool tasks (robot, hanoi, scales) the same way. Manual: watch 3 children 6-8 solve 3 tasks and note how many press Дальше within 5s vs scroll looking for it (target: no scroll hunting). Metric: share of solved tasks that are followed by a visible Feedback read (feedback in viewport >= 1s).
- **Review:** feasibility moderate, age fit True, manipulation risk low. The problem is real; I measured it at Pixel 7 on day1 task 1. RU success feedback spans y 702-802, but the bottom bar starts at y 770, so 32 px of the card is cut off. In UZ the retry card runs to 774, also clipped. The XP toast (274-396 x 779-823) lies exactly on top of 'Дальше' (284-396 x 783-827), as XpToast.tsx:38 (fixed right-4 bottom-4 z-50) predicts. Scroll margin, the toast move and the green 'Дальше' are good and cheap. Three parts do not hold up. (a) The chip '🤔 А ещё подумай' does not fit: at 412 px 'Назад' is about 108 px and 'Дальше' about 125 px, so with a 170 px chip plus gaps you need about 427 px, and UZ is longer. It also gives a second next action next to 'Дальше', against Hick's law. (b) A new 'hm' sound on every retry is a second audio event on top of the existing retry-1/2 voice clip. For a child who misses 3 times that is a repeated negative cue, even if soft. (c) The sfx facts are wrong: playSfx is gated by settings.boardSounds (a chess-board setting) and not by settings.sound (sfx.ts:~87), and 'collect' is one sweeping tone, not a two-note chime.

#### TASK-S2 · modify · effort S · impact 4 — Gender-neutral Russian copy sweep with an automated guard

- **Addresses:** TASK-2
- **Proposal:** Replace every masculine past-tense form addressed to the child with neutral wording (noun, impersonal verb, present tense, or imperative), without changing meaning, and add a unit test that fails when a new one appears. Known hits: AfterSolve.tsx:9-12 marks, DayFinish.tsx:50,60,61,64, HintLadder.tsx:59 'Застрял?', RobotPuzzle.tsx:233, GridPuzzles.tsx:279, WallLab.tsx:113, MagicTrianglePuzzle.tsx:236, ChessExercises.tsx:709 ('Ты нашёл все...'). Then run a repo-wide grep over ru strings (src/content/**, src/components/**, src/lib/feedback.ts) for patterns such as /\b(я|ты)\s+\S*(л|лся|лась)\b/i and \b(нашёл|объяснил|справился|поработал|застрял|догадался|решил|сдался|понял)\b, review the hits by hand (some are third person or are about a robot), and add a vitest/node test (tests/ru-gender.test.ts or a script in package.json 'lint:copy') with an allow-list. Uzbek strings stay as they are (no gender). Note: code strings use U+02BB for o' and g'; the Uzbek copy below uses plain apostrophes and must be converted to the project's character when pasted.
- **Revised after review:** Do the sweep in two passes. Pass 1 (UI components and followUps, no re-recording): all strings listed above plus the missed ones, with the same neutral patterns (noun, impersonal, imperative). Use number-first labels that agree grammatically, e.g. 'решений объяснено', 'других способов найдено'; replace 'подумать сам' with 'подумать'. Marks: 'Объяснение получилось', 'Нашёлся другой способ', 'Было трудно, но получилось'. Add tests/ru-gender.test.ts (vitest, same style as the name guard) with a regex over RU strings of src/components, src/lib/feedback.ts and content followUps, plus an allow-list for third-person and robot lines (e.g. 'Незнайка решил', 'Детектив нашёл', 'Робот не нашёл'). Pass 2: scan narrated task bodies; list hits and re-record only those clips, in the same batch as other voice work. Keep the parent-facing wording (ParentDayView, insights, review) separate: it is addressed to adults and may stay as is.
- **UI spec:** No layout change. Replacement table (RU -> new RU): 'Я объяснил решение' -> 'Объяснение получилось'; 'Я нашёл другой способ' -> 'Нашёлся другой способ'; 'Было трудно, но я справился' -> 'Было трудно, но получилось'; 'Понравилась задача' stays. DayFinish: 'Ты хорошо поработал! Посмотри, что сегодня получилось.' -> 'Хорошая работа! Посмотри, что сегодня получилось.'; stats 'объяснил решение' -> 'объяснений решений'; 'нашёл другой способ' -> 'других способов найдено'; 'не сдался в трудной' -> 'трудных задач пройдено до конца'. HintLadder: 'Застрял? Подсказки открываются по одной.' -> 'Нужна помощь? Подсказки открываются по одной.' Tools: 'Ты нашёл все пути!' -> 'Все пути найдены!'; 'Ты нашёл все числа' -> 'Все числа найдены!'. Where the child's name is shown, prefer 'Анна, ...' address in imperative.
- **Copy:** RU: Объяснение получилось / Нашёлся другой способ / Было трудно, но получилось / Хорошая работа! / Нужна помощь? / Все пути найдены! / UZ: Yechimni tushuntirdim / Boshqa usul topdim / Qiyin bo'ldi, lekin uddaladim / Yaxshi ish! / Yordam kerakmi? / Barcha yo'llar topildi!
- **Files:** src/components/task/AfterSolve.tsx, src/components/session/DayFinish.tsx, src/components/task/HintLadder.tsx, src/components/robot/RobotPuzzle.tsx, src/components/answers/GridPuzzles.tsx, src/components/answers/WallLab.tsx, src/components/answers/MagicTrianglePuzzle.tsx, src/components/chess/ChessExercises.tsx, src/lib/feedback.ts, package.json
- **Inspired by:** Owner's gender-neutral principle; process-focused praise (Mueller and Dweck, Hattie and Timperley: say what was done, not who the child is); Khan Kids/Duolingo ABC use short, subject-free feedback.
- **Guardrails:** Praise names an action or an outcome ('объяснение получилось'), never an ability ('умница', 'гений'). Do not add pressure words ('должен'). Keep the Russian natural: do not use clumsy slash forms like 'справился(ась)'. Check that the neutral lines still read well aloud, since recorded clips for feedback must be regenerated only where the spoken text changes.
- **Test plan:** Run the new copy test in CI (must fail on a planted 'я справился'). Run a one-time grep before/after and attach the list. Manual read of the 5 busiest screens (task, hint box, AfterSolve, finish, robot) with the test profile 'Анна' and a boy's name; ask one Russian-speaking parent of a girl and one of a boy whether anything sounds off. Audit count target: 0 masculine forms in child-facing RU copy.
- **Review:** feasibility easy, age fit True, manipulation risk none. The principle is right (owner rule, and process-praise evidence), and the existing guard-test precedent (tests/child-name.test.ts) makes a vitest check cheap. But the hit list is incomplete, so a 'known hits' approach would leave the product still gendered. Missing from the proposal: HintLadder.tsx:59 also says 'подумать сам' (masculine); NumberPuzzles.tsx:300 'Ты нашёл разные правила' and :393 'Я решил и рассказал взрослому'; DayFinish.tsx:108 'что нового ты сегодня понял?'; PrintSheets.tsx:132 'я сегодня понял' and PrintAnswerArea.tsx:465 'Что я заметил' (print styles); awards.ts:84 'Отметь «объяснил»'; and follow-up questions in content: week1/day7.ts:30 'Как ты справился?', week1/day4.ts:340 'ты нашёл ВСЕ', week1/day3.ts:88 'ты догадался', week1/day2.ts:444 'ты понял', week2/day4.ts:35, week3/day2.ts:89. The proposed stat labels are also awkward, because Stat shows a big number then the label ('объяснений решений' next to 1 reads wrongly). Finally, narrated task bodies and question blocks are hash-bound to recordings (voiceText.ts, tests/voice.test.ts), so any edit inside task bodies forces ElevenLabs re-recording; follow-ups and UI strings do not.

#### TASK-S3 · modify · effort M · impact 4 — Task-aware retry: echo the child's answer, one short next step, authored 'common slips'

- **Addresses:** TASK-4
- **Proposal:** Replace the generic retry card for number/text fields with a three-part micro-feedback built on Hattie and Timperley's 'where next': (1) echo: a chip shows what the child entered ('Твой ответ: 50') so the card is clearly about this attempt; (2) one short sentence (max 8 words in RU) that names where to look, from an authored 'slip' if the answer matches a known wrong idea, else from a per-task default 'look here' line, else from a short generic pool; (3) two big buttons: 'Ещё раз' (focuses the field) and '💡 Подсказка' (opens/scrolls to the ladder, visible from the first miss, not only after two). Add an optional field to the content type: slips?: {when: string|number|RegExp-string; ru: string; uz: string}[] and lookHere?: {ru; uz}. Author slips for the 40 highest-traffic tasks first (week 1 days 1-3, all 'fields' tasks that appear in the audit), e.g. 19+19+19: 50 -> '20+20+10? Попробуй сложить 19 и 19 сначала'. Fix the duplicated emoji (RETRY_TITLE contains 🤔 and ICONS adds it, feedback.ts:28 vs Feedback.tsx:23). Never reveal the correct value or say hot/cold (that would invite guess-and-check). Cap the sentence length so Aziz can hear it: add the generic retry clips (they exist via cheer('retry')) and play the sentence clip only when a recorded line exists.
- **Revised after review:** Phase A (small, do now): remove the emoji from RETRY_TITLE, replace the 4 rotating titles with 2 stable short ones, shorten retry subs to at most 8 words in RU and UZ, and add the echo chip 'Твой ответ: 50' only (no buttons). Keep the hint pointer as a text line after the 2nd miss (already exists) and let S12's header button carry hint access. Phase B (data first): locally log the wrong numeric values per task (small capped list) visible in the parent area; after a pilot, author slips only for tasks where one wrong value recurs. Slip type: {when: number | number[]; ru; uz}. A per-task lookHere line is optional. Never show the right value or hot/cold. Keep unlimited retries and no counter shown to the child.
- **UI spec:** Retry card (sun-soft) layout, 412px wide: row 1 icon 🤔 (no emoji in the title text) + title 'Пока не сходится' (rotation reduced to 3 short titles); row 2 echo chip: white pill, 'Твой ответ: 50', 18px bold; row 3 the one-line next step, 18px; row 4 two buttons side by side, each min-h-14, 'Ещё раз' (secondary, auto-focus the input and select its text) and '💡 Подсказка' (soft). After the 2nd miss the sub-line adds 'Можно открыть подсказку' only if not already visible; after 3 misses on the same wrong value add 'Давай разберём вместе?' with a link to the ladder. Animation: card slides in 150ms; the input briefly shakes 2px (reduced motion off). Content type change in src/content/types.ts; FieldsAnswer.tsx:40-50 passes values to feedback.
- **Copy:** RU: Пока не сходится. | Твой ответ: 50 | Посмотри ещё раз на первое сложение. | [Ещё раз] [💡 Подсказка] / UZ: Hozircha mos kelmadi. | Javobing: 50 | Birinchi qo'shishga yana bir qara. | [Yana bir bor] [💡 Maslahat]
- **Files:** src/lib/feedback.ts, src/components/answers/Feedback.tsx, src/components/answers/FieldsAnswer.tsx, src/components/answers/ChoiceAnswers.tsx, src/content/types.ts, src/content/week1/day1.ts, src/components/task/HintLadder.tsx
- **Inspired by:** Desmos 'interpretive feedback' (replay the child's idea) and Hattie and Timperley's feed-up/feed-back/feed-forward; Khan Academy Kids non-verbal tilt-head cue; owner's 'no wrong' rule.
- **Guardrails:** No 'wrong', red, buzzer, or lost-point wording. Do not show 'closer/farther' or the right value, which would turn it into guess-and-check; keep unlimited retries with no counter shown to the child. The hint button is a normal, equal-weight control and using it costs nothing (see TASK-S12). Authored slips must be reviewed by a Uzbek and a Russian speaker; fallback must never be longer than the old text.
- **Test plan:** Unit test: for each authored slip, feeding the slip value returns that slip text; unknown value returns lookHere; no output string contains 'неправильно|ошибк|xato'. Playwright: type 50 on day1-t1, assert echo chip text, assert 'Ещё раз' focuses input, assert no duplicate emoji. Measure retry-to-solve: median number of attempts per task and hint-open rate after first miss (expect up), via local analytics counters in the parent area or manual sessions with 3 children. UZ check at 412px: no overflow on the two buttons.
- **Review:** feasibility moderate, age fit False, manipulation risk low. Fixing the duplicated emoji and the empty 'Какая часть решения точно верная?' for single-number fields is clearly right (confirmed in retry-ru.png: 🤔 icon and 🤔 in the title). The full redesign, however, adds a lot. The retry card grows from about 77 px to roughly 220 px (echo chip, sentence, two 56 px buttons), which on a 412x839 page lands entirely behind the 69 px bottom bar and pushes the actual 'try again' field out of sight; it also adds reading load for Aziz. 'Ещё раз' is redundant: the field is right above. Showing a hint button from the first miss lowers productive struggle, although hintPause defaults to true. Authoring 40 'slips' by guessing is speculative: the app never records wrong values (store only keeps missed counts), so we do not know which wrong answers are common. 'when' as RegExp does not survive the server-to-client content pass. And it needs reviewed RU and UZ copy for every slip.

#### TASK-S4 · drop · effort M · impact 4 — Kid number pad instead of the system keyboard for number answers (ages 6-9)

- **Addresses:** TASK-3, TASK-11
- **Proposal:** For tasks whose fields are numbers (about 99 of 165), render an in-page number pad for juniors and middles (ageProfile in src/lib/age.ts, default on for age < 10, setting 'Экранные цифры' in parent settings for others). The input becomes readOnly with inputMode='none' so the Android keyboard never covers the task. Pad: 3x4 grid (1-9, ⌫, 0, ✓) docked inside the answer card (not fixed), keys 64px high x ~96px wide, 8px gaps, tap feedback with 3D press like Button. The ✓ key is the Проверить action (the separate 'Проверить' button stays for screen readers and Enter, hidden visually on junior). For multi-field tasks, tapping a field makes it active (ring), the pad types into it, ✓ moves to the next empty field then checks. Minus key appears only if the task allows negatives; time/coord fields keep their own controls. Seniors (age >=10, Dilnoza) keep the native keyboard unless they switch.
- **UI spec:** Answer card on phone: field (h-16, text-3xl, shows '?' placeholder) then the pad 3 columns, total height about 4x64+3x8 = 280px. To keep goal and controls visible together, the task body stays above and the pad scrolls into view once (scrollIntoView nearest) when the first field is tapped. Keys: mint ✓ at bottom-right (success variant), ⌫ at bottom-left (secondary). Key press: translateY 2px, 80ms; haptic navigator.vibrate(8) if available. Max 5 digits like the current slice(0,5). Landscape/tablet: pad width max 320px, centred. Accessible names: each key 'цифра 7', ⌫ 'стереть', ✓ 'проверить'.
- **Files:** src/components/answers/FieldsAnswer.tsx, src/components/answers/NumPad.tsx, src/lib/age.ts, src/lib/state.ts, src/components/parent/ParentSettings.tsx
- **Inspired by:** NN/g young-user guidance (big targets, tap over type, a system keyboard hides the question); Khan Academy Kids and Matific custom keypads; Sesame Workshop tap-first findings.
- **Guardrails:** The pad must not add speed pressure (no timer, no key-repeat rewards). It must not enable fast brute-force guessing beyond what exists: no extra sound loops on each press. Keep the native-keyboard path for children who prefer it and for parents (setting persists in settings, not behind a PIN, but described honestly). Do not store anything new about the child other than a boolean setting.
- **Test plan:** Playwright Pixel 7 day1-t1 for age 7: assert no virtual keyboard (visualViewport height unchanged after focus), pad keys >=64px high, tapping 5 then 7 then ✓ gives the success feedback, ⌫ removes. Check targets with the audit script (small44 for this page should drop). Multi-field task (e.g. two fields) active-field flow. Manual: time 5 children to enter a 2-digit answer with keyboard vs pad (expect fewer mis-taps and faster time to Проверить). Check Enter key still works on desktop.
- **Review:** feasibility hard, age fit False, manipulation risk none. The premise is that a custom pad keeps the question visible, but the geometry does not allow it. On Pixel 7 the answer card starts near y 455 and the field sits around y 520-620 (kid7-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg). A 280 px pad then runs to about y 920, behind the bottom bar (starts y 770). The spec admits it must scroll the pad into view, which scrolls the question off screen, the very problem the system keyboard causes. Gboard's numeric keyboard already has about 56-60 dp keys, so the gain in key size is small, while the pad adds 280 px to every typed task and pushes Feedback even lower (worsening TASK-1). The spec also contradicts itself: it says seniors are 'age >= 10, Dilnoza', but ageProfile makes 9-10 'middle' and senior starts at 11 (age.ts, tests/age.test.ts). Effort is understated: readOnly inputs break Playwright fill() in e2e/smoke.spec.ts:39,47 and others, multi-field, time and coord tasks need separate handling, and screen-reader behaviour changes. TASK-3's 'no number pad made for the child' is an assertion, not an observed failure.

#### TASK-S5 · modify · effort L · impact 4 — Vary the verb: three light tap-based answer types replace about 25 typed tasks

- **Addresses:** TASK-3
- **Proposal:** Add three small, reusable answer kinds that need no typing and convert about 25 of the 99 'fields' tasks (start with weeks 1-2, tasks 1-3 of each day, because that is where Aziz starts and where the first-days pattern is set): (a) 'numberline' - a draggable-or-tappable pin on a number line with snap, for ordering/estimate/'which number' tasks; (b) 'counters' - tap-to-add blocks/ten-frame grouped in 5s and 10s, the number is read from the structure, for addition/subtraction/multiplication-as-groups; (c) 'pick' - 3-4 big picture-or-number cards (extends the existing choice kind with larger tiles and images from src/components/visuals). Each gives a visible goal state that lights up on success. Rule for the day plan: no day may have more than 4 consecutive typed fields tasks and the first two tasks must use at least two different kinds; add this as a content lint in a script. All three support tap-to-place first and optional drag (tap select then tap place), so no drag-only interaction exists. Result is persisted in the same task progress record so checks, hints and XP continue to work.
- **Revised after review:** Pilot two new answer kinds only: 'numberline' (tap to place a pin with snap) and 'tenFrame' (tap cells, grouped 5/10, total shown). Convert 8-10 tasks in week 1 day 1-3 and week 2 day 1-3 where the maths really is number-line or grouping, not just any addition. Each converted task keeps its typed fields as the answer for ages 9+ (altAnswer by ageProfile) and keeps its follow-ups. Do not add 'pick' for computed answers; extend ChoiceAnswer visuals instead where a task is already a choice. Add the content lint 'first two tasks of a day use at least two kinds' and run it as a vitest. Measure session length and completion over 2 weeks before converting more.
- **UI spec:** numberline: track 340px wide, 56px pin, labelled ticks every 5 or 10, snapped; the selected value is shown in a 48px bubble above the pin; 'Проверить' stays. counters: 10-frame grid 2x5 cells 52px, tap fills a cell, tap again removes; bank of 'ещё 1' and 'ещё 5' buttons 56px; running total hidden for tasks that ask 'сколько' (to prevent counter-as-answer) but shown as grouping lines. pick: tiles min-h-20, 2 columns at 412px, selected ring + check icon, nothing is submitted until Проверить. Animation: pin slides 120ms; counters pop 100ms; success tiles glow mint, retry tiles do not turn red (sun outline only).
- **Files:** src/components/answers/AnswerPanel.tsx, src/components/answers/NumberLinePin.tsx, src/components/answers/CountersAnswer.tsx, src/components/answers/ChoiceAnswers.tsx, src/content/types.ts, src/content/week1/day1.ts, src/content/week1/day2.ts, scripts/lint-day-variety.mjs
- **Inspired by:** Desmos 'vary the verb' and 'easy to start, hard to finish'; DragonBox/Mathigon/Polypad virtual manipulatives and concreteness fading; Khan Academy Kids tap-first interaction.
- **Guardrails:** Manipulatives must not become game decoration that replaces the maths (DragonBox study): each converted task keeps its follow-up 'А ещё подумай'. No timers, no stars-per-speed. Counters must not let the child tap-spam to reach the answer without thinking: no running total on 'сколько' tasks. Drag is optional, never required. Do not convert tasks that really need a typed derivation for ages 10+ (keep a 'ввести число' fallback toggle for seniors).
- **Test plan:** Count answer kinds before/after via the grep used in the audit (target: fields <= 75 of ~165). Content lint passes for all 21 days. Unit tests for each answer type's check function (correct, near, empty). Playwright: complete one converted task by tap only, on touch emulation, and by keyboard. Manual with 3-5 children aged 6-10: observe whether the 2nd half of a day still holds attention (count tasks completed in a 15-minute session).
- **Review:** feasibility hard, age fit True, manipulation risk none. Varying the verb and concreteness fading are well supported, and the data confirm that the opening is monotone: week 1 day 1 is F F A F R sym F F, week 2 day 1 is F F F F R F F F, day 2 and 3 likewise (kind order read from src/content). But the proposal is oversized and partly harmful. 'Pick' is just ChoiceAnswer with larger tiles (it already supports shape and polyomino visuals), so it is not a new kind. Converting computed-answer tasks to 3-4 picture cards turns recall into recognition with a 25-33% guess chance, which weakens learning and invites guess-and-check, against S3's own guardrails. The 'counters' design hides the running total on 'сколько' tasks, which is confusing for a child who is just counting by tapping. Converting 25 tasks removes typed practice that ages 9-12 (Dilnoza) still need, and the content is not age-specific, so each converted task would need a typed fallback for middle/senior (two answer specs per task, in RU and UZ). The lint rule 'max 4 consecutive typed' is already met by the current content (longest run is 4), so only the 'first two tasks differ' part would bite. L effort for impact the proposal itself calls 4 is not justified before a pilot.

#### TASK-S6 · modify · effort M · impact 4 — Tools keep goal and controls in one viewport: sticky board, compact chrome on phones

- **Addresses:** TASK-5
- **Proposal:** For the interactive tools (robot, Hanoi, scales, number machine, crossing) split the layout on screens under 640px into a sticky 'stage' (the board with goal: flag, scales, pegs) and a scrolling 'controls' area underneath. The stage is position: sticky just below the header, with a white card background and a soft shadow, at most 42% of the viewport height (board cell size computed from visualViewport.height minus chrome minus controls). The robot's arrow pad, program and feedback scroll under it, so the flag is always visible while pressing arrows, and after a successful run the robot sits visibly on the flag. In the same pass shrink phone chrome: bottom nav 68 -> 60px (and see TASK-S14 for the header), and hide the header on scroll down / show on scroll up for tool tasks. Add a 'Показать цель' pulse on the flag when the child presses Запустить with an empty program. Desktop is unchanged.
- **Revised after review:** Phase 1: robot only (and Hanoi if it works). Make the board wrapper sticky below the header using a CSS variable for the header height, with a viewport-height guard (non-sticky if viewport < 700 px or bigText, or if stage + controls > 85% of the viewport). Shrink robot cells only if needed (arrows are already 48 px, board cells about 56 px). No header hide-on-scroll, no bottom-nav resize, no flag pulse (S11 handles the empty-program message). Measure with the proposed Playwright test (flag bbox inside viewport before and after Запустить) at 412x839 and 360x640, and watch for scroll jank on a real mid-range Android. Extend to other tools only if phase 1 works.
- **UI spec:** Phone 412x839: header (after S14) about 64px; sticky stage top: 64px, height <= 300px (4-row robot board at 56px cells = 224px + 8px padding); arrows pad 3x2 grid of 56px buttons below, program strip below that; feedback card appears directly under the stage-adjacent controls and scrolls into view above the 60px bottom nav. Stage has a 1px bottom line to show it is pinned. Hanoi: pegs in the stage, move counter and records below. Scales: the balance is in the stage, weight tray scrolls. If the viewport height < 640px (small phones, landscape), the stage becomes non-sticky and the board shrinks to 48px cells. Reduced motion: no slide on header hide.
- **Files:** src/components/robot/RobotPuzzle.tsx, src/components/robot/RobotBoard.tsx, src/components/answers/HanoiPuzzle.tsx, src/components/answers/ScalesPuzzle.tsx, src/components/answers/CrossingPuzzle.tsx, src/components/session/DaySession.tsx
- **Inspired by:** Fitts/proximity and 'no hidden state'; NN/g: children avoid scrolling; Toca/Sago Mini-style direct-manipulation toys where the toy stays on screen; Khan Kids tool screens.
- **Guardrails:** No new gestures or hidden panels: the stage is just always visible. Do not auto-run or auto-solve; do not add timers. Keep an obvious way to see the whole task text (it stays above, scrollable). Test with 'bigText' on so the sticky stage does not eat the whole screen (fallback to non-sticky when stage + controls > 85% of viewport).
- **Test plan:** Playwright Pixel 7 robot task: press an arrow, assert the flag element's bbox is inside the viewport and above the arrows (not clipped by header or bottom nav) before and after Запустить. Same for Hanoi and scales. Run audit-metrics script: no new horizontal overflow, aboveFoldInteractive does not drop. Test at 360x640 and with bigText. Manual: ask a child to guide the robot to the flag and count scrolls (target: zero scrolls between first arrow and result).
- **Review:** feasibility moderate, age fit True, manipulation risk none. The pain point is real: in rich-phone-day1-robot-t1/t2 the flag row is at the top of the board while the arrow pad sits roughly 330 px lower, so the goal is not visible while pressing arrows. But the proposal bundles five features and each is risky. A sticky 260-300 px stage under a 112 px header plus a 69 px bottom bar leaves only about 330-400 px of scroll area on an 839 px viewport, and real Chrome with URL bar is shorter than 839, so arrows, program, run buttons and feedback may not all fit. The sticky offset must equal the header height, which differs (112 now, varies with S14, bigText, and SiteHeader), so it needs a measured CSS variable. Hide-on-scroll header adds motion and 'hidden panel' behaviour that contradicts the stated 'no hidden state' guardrail. Each of the five tools (robot, Hanoi, scales, crossing, number machine) has a different structure, so 'M' is optimistic. The flag-pulse on empty Запустить duplicates S11.

#### TASK-S7 · modify · effort M · impact 5 — Audio-first for pre-readers: a big speaker button, one-time auto-read after a tap, audio on hints

- **Addresses:** TASK-6
- **Proposal:** Make narration the first, biggest control for juniors (ageProfile 'junior', age 6-8), and available on hints. (1) Move the listen control out of the chip row (TaskView.tsx:55-57) into its own full-width row directly under the title: a 56px high pill 'Послушать' with a speaker icon and an animated 3-bar sound wave while playing (stop toggle). Middles get a 44px pill; seniors keep today's small chip. Fix the UZ wrap by giving the button its own row. (2) 'Читать вслух сам' setting (default ON for juniors, OFF for others, in child settings): after any user tap on the page (tapping Начать or Дальше satisfies browser autoplay rules, sfxUnlock already exists), the task clip plays once automatically on opening a task; a visible mute button stops it; never plays twice for the same task in the same session; never plays when settings.sound is false. If audio is blocked, the button pulses once with a 'Нажми, чтобы послушать' tooltip. (3) Hints: each hint card gets a 44px icon-only speaker (phase 1: generate clips for hint rung 1 and 2 of the 55 week-1 tasks; later all) using the existing ElevenLabs pipeline and voice-clips.json (extend VOICE_CLIPS with .hint(taskId, n, lang)); where a clip is absent, no button is shown (no browser speech, per owner rule). (4) The day-finish page and day intro get one summary clip each (name-free). (5) Lazy-load and cache audio: the service worker should serve /audio/ mp3 with range support from a cache (public/sw.js:41 currently skips mp3), limited to the active language and to clips that were already played.
- **Revised after review:** Ship in two steps. Step 1: for junior, the listen control becomes its own full-width 56 px row directly under the title (own row also fixes the UZ wrap of 'Oʻqib berish'), with a simple playing state (stop toggle; bars animation off under reduced motion). Middle gets 44 px, senior keeps the chip. Add a 'Читать задачи вслух' setting (child gear and parent settings), default ON for junior only if sound is on. Auto-read happens once per task per session, only after a user gesture, never for the next task automatically, never when sound is off; if play() is blocked the button pulses once. Step 2 (after a pilot with 3 children aged 6-7): hint clips for rungs 2-3 of week 1, via the existing recording workflow. Remove the SW range-caching item from this proposal and handle it as a separate offline task. Day-finish clip belongs to S9 only.
- **UI spec:** Listen row: pill bg brand-soft, border-2 brand/30, 56px high, 'Послушать' 18px bold + speaker 28px; playing state: bg brand, white, 3 animated bars (CSS, 0.9s loop, stops with reduced motion), label 'Стоп'. Auto-read toast: none; instead the pill shows playing state immediately. Hint speaker: 44x44 icon button at the card's top-right. Setting row in parent settings and in the child's gear: 'Читать задачи вслух' toggle. Desktop keeps the chip variant for seniors.
- **Files:** src/components/task/TaskView.tsx, src/components/ListenButton.tsx, src/components/task/HintLadder.tsx, src/lib/voice.ts, src/lib/state.ts, src/components/session/DayFinish.tsx, public/sw.js, src/components/parent/ParentSettings.tsx
- **Inspired by:** Khan Academy Kids and Sesame (voice-first, speaker as the largest control); Duolingo ABC read-aloud; NN/g (the youngest do not read; audio can fail silently so give a visible state); cognitive load theory for slow decoders.
- **Guardrails:** Autoplay only after a user gesture, only once per task, and always with a visible stop; no autoplay of the next task or of any praise loop; respect settings.sound and the 'quiet mode'. Audio is informational, not a reward. Never use browser speech synthesis (owner's rule). Do not pre-download the whole 80 MB library on mobile data; cache what was played and let a parent opt in to a week pack later. Name-free recorded lines only.
- **Test plan:** Playwright: for a junior profile the listen row is >=56px high and above the first body paragraph; clicking it sets aria-pressed=true; autoplay respects sound=false and does not fire without a prior gesture (mock Audio.play). Run the audit script for noName. Check UZ at 412px that the button does not wrap. Manual with 3 children aged 6-7: how many find and press the speaker without prompting within 10s of opening task 1 (target 3/3 vs the current button). Measure service-worker cache size after one session (should be a few MB) and replay of a clip offline.
- **Review:** feasibility moderate, age fit True, manipulation risk none. Audio-first for 6-8 is the strongest idea in the batch. The current button is small (122x36 px, kid7-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg), pale, and sits in a chip row. Recorded clips exist for all 165 tasks in RU and UZ (voice-clips.json: 165 tasks, 52 dyk, 23 lessons each), so a big speaker row and optional auto-read have real content to use. Age gating matters because narration alongside text helps emergent readers but can hurt fluent ones (expertise reversal), so juniors only is right. Problems: (1) auto-read default ON can surprise a parent in public on a shared phone; make the first auto-read follow an explicit choice. (2) Hint audio is only available for rung 1-2 in the proposal, but rung 1 is mostly 'Прочитай ещё раз', so it has the least value. (3) The service-worker change is unrelated to the UI and risky: Cache API with range requests is not trivial, and sw.js:49 skips mp3 deliberately. (4) Day-finish clips duplicate S9's voice line. (5) Hints with hash-bound clips need regeneration whenever text changes (voiceText.ts and voice.test.ts).

#### TASK-S8 · drop · effort L · impact 3 — Hint audio pack and text-light hints for Aziz (content and pipeline)

- **Addresses:** TASK-6
- **Proposal:** Generate recorded hint clips (RU and UZ) for the first two rungs of every task, then the rest, using the ElevenLabs workflow that produced voice-clips.json. Shorten hint texts for juniors: rungs get a `short` variant (max about 12 words) in the content type, shown instead of the long text when ageProfile is junior, and where possible rungs 3-5 act on the tool (robot greys out the first two arrows, scales pre-place one weight) instead of describing. A script (scripts/build-hint-voice.mjs, new) reads the content, hashes each string, and generates only changed clips, so edits do not regenerate everything. This is the content half of TASK-S7; the UI hook (.hint(taskId, n, lang)) is in S7.
- **UI spec:** No new layout beyond S7's hint speaker. Hint card for juniors shows `short` text at 20px, the full text behind a 'Подробнее' link (44px). For tool tasks a rung can carry `action: 'ghost-first-moves' | 'preplace-weight'` rendered as a faded preview on the board with the label 'Вот первый шаг' - the child still completes it.
- **Files:** src/content/types.ts, src/content/week1/day1.ts, src/components/task/HintLadder.tsx, src/lib/voice.ts, scripts/build-hint-voice.mjs, public/audio
- **Inspired by:** Khan Academy Kids animated step-by-step walkthrough for help; the arXiv tutoring study cited in the digest (last rung is a partly worked step in the workspace); Desmos: short expository screens.
- **Guardrails:** The last rung must never give the final answer; hint text stays process-focused. Hints stay one-by-one with the pause setting. Clips must be name-free. Budget the audio size (target under 1.5 MB per week-pack of rung 1-2 clips) and lazy-load; do not make the app dependent on audio to work.
- **Test plan:** Content test: every task has hints[0].short in RU and UZ for week 1; script is idempotent (second run generates 0 clips). Check audio duration < 8s per hint clip. Playwright: junior profile sees short text and speaker; senior sees full text. Manual listening review of 20 clips by a native Uzbek and a native Russian speaker. Track hint-open rate and solve-after-hint rate for week 1 across a pilot.
- **Review:** feasibility hard, age fit True, manipulation risk none. The premise that hints are too long for juniors is not supported by the data. In week 1 the average hint is 12.5 words (275 hints; 123 of them are over 12 words, but the first two rungs of the sampled tasks are 7-14 words, e.g. 'Прочитай пример ещё раз. Сколько раз в нём повторяется число 19?'). Writing a `short` variant for 275+ hints in two languages is a lot of content work for small gain. 'Ghost first moves' and 'preplace-weight' actions are bespoke features per tool (robot, scales), which is a different, large project, and they partly reveal the solution. A new scripts/build-hint-voice.mjs cannot import the TS content without a loader (scripts are .mjs; current voice clips were recorded through the ElevenLabs workflow, and the manifest is written by a vitest run). Its value depends on S7 step 2 pilot results, which do not exist yet. Effort L, impact 3.

#### TASK-S9 · modify · effort M · impact 5 — A real end-of-day: celebration first, honest summary, one clear next step, reflection optional

- **Addresses:** TASK-7
- **Proposal:** Rebuild DayFinish as two short beats. Beat 1, 'Celebrate' (the whole page for juniors): a 2-second skippable animation (the day's emoji or a sparkle burst, CSS only, no libraries), a row of solved stars (filled for solved, outlined for not yet; no zero count shame), '+20 XP' and the XP level bar moving, the 'week dots' row from gentleStreak/weekActiveDays (quest.ts), the day's thinking habit badge, and exactly two equal-size buttons: 'Следующий день →' (primary) and 'Домой'. Pressing either marks the day completed (today it only happens on 'Завершить день' and then routes home, DayFinish.tsx:36-39), so 'next day' is available immediately. Beat 2, 'Tell us' (below the fold for juniors, inline for seniors): a single optional prompt with the 4 moods (14px labels) for juniors; seniors (Dilnoza) also get favourite and hardest task pickers, and a 'share my result' card (private image, first name only, no ranking). Honest copy by tier: 0 solved -> 'Сегодня только заглянули. Вернёмся к задачам?' with primary 'К задачам', no XP, no congratulation and 'Завершить' hidden; 1-4 solved -> 'Хорошая работа! Остальные ждут тебя в любой день.'; all solved -> 'Все задачи дня решены!' with a bigger burst. Play one name-free recorded line (new clip 'finish-1..3') after the animation.
- **Revised after review:** Beat 1 for all: CSS-only 1.5-2 s skippable burst (reduced-motion: static), stars for solved tasks (outline for the rest, no zero shaming), '+20 XP · Уровень N' with the bar, week dots (empty circles, never red), the day's habit. Tiers: 0 solved = 'Сегодня только заглянули. Вернёмся к задачам?' with 'К задачам', no XP, day not completable; 1-7 solved = 'Хорошая работа! Остальные ждут в любой день.'; all solved = 'Все задачи дня решены!'. Two buttons of equal size and weight: 'Готово ✓' (marks completedAt, home) and 'Следующий день →' (marks completedAt, opens next). No button marks the day when 0 are solved. Change xpTotal so day XP needs at least 1 solved task. Beat 2 below the fold: mood row for everyone (labels at least 14 px); favourite/hardest pickers for middle and senior only. Drop the PNG share card. A name-free finish clip can be added later via the voice workflow.
- **UI spec:** Phone: hero card 412px wide, emoji 72px bouncing in once (scale 0.6 -> 1.1 -> 1, 500ms), stars row 8 stars 32px wrapped in 2 rows of 4 if day has 8 tasks (or one row of 8 at 40px - choose 8 x 40px with 4px gap = 352px), confetti: 12 CSS dots, 1.6s, prefers-reduced-motion off. XP: bar from previous level progress animating to new in 700ms, text '+20 XP · Уровень 3'. Week dots: 7 circles 24px, current day ringed; label 'Эта неделя: 3 дня'. Buttons stacked, each min-h-14 full width, equal size. Below: 'Хочешь поделиться впечатлением? (по желанию)' collapsible. 'Skip' = tap anywhere on animation. Seniors: a 'Мой результат' card to save as PNG via canvas, containing the first name only, day title, solved count and XP, no rating numbers.
- **Files:** src/components/session/DayFinish.tsx, src/lib/quest.ts, src/lib/xp.ts, src/lib/store.ts, src/app/globals.css, src/lib/voice.ts
- **Inspired by:** Peak-end rule; Duolingo round-complete celebration (one per round, not per tap); Khan Kids / Lingokids star and sticker accumulation; Dilnoza's need to show progress (private certificate card, no leaderboard).
- **Guardrails:** No loss wording on the weekly dots (they only fill up; gap days are empty circles, not red); no countdown or 'come back tomorrow or lose...'; the hook is a neutral 'Завтра: День N - название' teaser. No XP shown as a payment before the task. Do not praise ability; praise the specific actions counted today. Reflection is optional and skippable; closing the page without answering saves nothing negative. Keep zero-solved honest (no false congratulation).
- **Test plan:** Playwright: open /week/1/day/1#finish with 0, 3 and 8 solved states seeded in localStorage; assert copy tier, star counts, button count = 2 with equal width, and that 'Следующий день' navigates and sets completedAt. Reduced motion run. Check RU and UZ at 412px for overflow. Measure: share of finished days that proceed to next day in a pilot (before: 'next' hidden on first visit), time on finish page (target under 30s for juniors), plus parent interview 'did your child seem proud?'.
- **Review:** feasibility moderate, age fit True, manipulation risk low. The diagnosis is accurate: DayFinish.tsx:36-39 calls updateDay(completedAt) then router.push('/'), so 'Следующий день →' (shown only when nextDayHref && done) cannot be seen the first time; the page can open at 0/8 and still say 'Ты хорошо поработал!'. A tiered, honest finish with a short celebration, XP and week dots is good. Points to fix. (1) completedAt feeds XP (+20, xp.ts:35) and activityDays/streak (awards.ts:264), so today a child can press 🏁 then 'Завершить' at 0/8 and earn 20 XP and a streak day for nothing; the proposed tiers must also stop completedAt (and its XP) when 0 tasks are solved. (2) Marking the day complete on either button changes semantics: a child peeking at the finish page and pressing 'Домой' would complete the day, and HomeDashboard.tsx:36 picks the 'next' day as the first without completedAt, so a day with 7 unsolved tasks would be skipped. (3) A primary 'Следующий день →' right after a full junior day (about 25 minutes) pushes continuation, against Aziz's 10-minute attention and the parent's wish for short sessions (and against S17). (4) The 'share my result' PNG with the child's name is scope creep and a privacy surface; there is already a printable certificate for chess.
