Short sessions with a built-in finish line** (verified; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/childrens-websites-usability-issues/ (NN/g, opened) for children's behaviour; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/childrens-information/childrens-code-guidance-and-resources/age-appropriate-design-a-code-of-practice-for-online-services/13-nudge-techniques/ (ICO Standard 13, opened) for break nudges) — NN/g found children want instant gratification, skip long instruction paragraphs, avoid scrolling, explore by clicking around, and need separate design for 6-8 and 9-12. The ICO standard says to nudge toward wellbeing behaviours such as taking breaks and to provide mid-level pause-and-save features. I found no traceable primary source for any 'age + N minutes' or 'N minutes per year' attention rule. Search summaries called it an untraceable rule of thumb that mainly applies to non-engaging tasks, so treat the 10 minutes for Aziz as the owner's design budget, not a research fact. _Why:_ Short, complete loops give an early win and a clean stopping point. Open-ended feeds do the opposite. _For Davlatjon:_ The kid7 home hero says '8 задач · около 25 минут' for one day (kid7-phone-home-t1.jpg). For ages 6-8 split a day into 3 mini-sessions of about 3 tasks ('Часть 1 из 3') with a clear 'На сегодня хватит' screen, the progress saved, and a parent-friendly 'вернёмся завтра'. Cap the daily quest at 3 items. Add a soft break prompt after about 15-20 minutes of continuous play ('Давай потянемся!') without a guilt message. Avoid autoplay of the next puzzle for under-10s, offering 'ещё одну?' as an explicit choice. Keep the fold uncluttered: /chess phone page has a ratio of 7.5 screens and /chess/history 13.5 (audit-metrics.json), which means long scroll for a group that avoids scrolling.
- **12. Concrete before abstract: manipulatives, then symbols** (unverified; background knowledge (Piaget's concrete-operational stage roughly 7-11; stage ages are approximate and much criticised). The NN/g age-band finding above is verified.) — Children in the concrete-operational range reason well about physical, manipulable situations and struggle with purely symbolic or hypothetical ones. Davlatjon's tools (balance scales, number machines, Hanoi, robot programmer, interactive chess board) are concrete manipulatives. _Why:_ Dragging, balancing and watching a robot run give the child a model of the idea before the notation arrives. _For Davlatjon:_ Sequence each topic as: act on objects, see the effect, name the idea, then write the symbol. Show chess notation and coordinates as a late layer; hide it for 6-8 (the /chess/coordinates trainer and notation views can stay behind a 'for older players' label). Make draggable objects at least 44 px and add tap-to-select as an alternative to drag, since precise dragging is hard at 6-8 (NN/g summary). Reuse the same tool across weeks with growing difficulty, so the child does not relearn the interface.
- **13. A forgiving streak that is a weekly rhythm, not a daily debt** (verified; https://blog.duolingo.com/how-duolingo-streak-builds-habit (Duolingo blog, opened)) — Duolingo's own post: streak freezes allow a paused day, equipping up to two freezes increased daily active learners by +0.38% (relative), a 7-day streak is associated with 3.6x course completion (correlation), a milestone animation raised new-learner 7-day retention by +1.7%, and the post itself says losing a streak can feel demotivating and fear of losing one could stop people attempting it. Loss aversion is the stated mechanism for long streaks. The post does not isolate loss aversion experimentally. _Why:_ A visible chain helps habit formation, but the loss framing carries emotional cost, which matters more for children. _For Davlatjon:_ The owner's 'gentle streak' is the right default. Strengthen it: count 'days played this week' (for example 3 of 7 lights), not consecutive days, so a missed day never zeroes anything. Auto-grant a free rest day. Never show a broken-streak message. Celebrate the milestone with an animation and a short recorded line. Show Dilnoza a week-and-month calendar with medals. Do not send push reminders that mention loss.

Anti-patterns:

- Loot boxes, mystery chests or randomised rewards tied to purchases or to play time — Variable-ratio schedules produce persistent responding (Skinner, background knowledge). Zendle, Meyer and Over 2019 (search summary, not opened) found loot-box spending linked to problem gambling in 16-18-year-olds, a correlation only. The ICO audit toolkit page (surfaced by search, not opened) asks for minimal loot-box use and odds disclosure. If surprise is used at all, restrict it to free content (a fun fact, a sticker) that is not purchasable, not tied to playing longer, and whose odds are never hidden.
- Streak-loss shame and guilt mascots ('your streak is dying', a sad owl) — Loss aversion is explicitly part of streak design. Duolingo's own post admits fear of losing a streak can deter starting one. For children it also makes a parent-run device a source of anxiety. Use celebratory framing and free rest days instead.
- Public ranking and leaderboards for under-10s — Social comparison turns learning into a status contest and demotivates the bottom half. The owner already hides ratings for under-10s, which is correct. For Dilnoza use personal bests and private challenges.
- Expected, tangible or time-based rewards ('play 30 minutes to earn a prize') — Deci, Koestner and Ryan 1999 (opened): expected tangible and engagement-contingent rewards reduced later free-choice interest (d about -0.40 for engagement-contingent), with larger harm for children. Time-based rewards also reward screen time, not learning.
- Intelligence or identity praise ('Genius!', 'You are so smart') — Mueller and Dweck 1998 (secondary summary): intelligence-praised fifth graders chose easier tasks, enjoyed tasks less and did worse after failure. The broader mindset literature is contested (Macnamara and Burgoyne d=0.05), but this particular praise is cheap to avoid and carries no information.
- Fake urgency: countdown timers, expiring offers, 'only today' quests — The ICO audit toolkit (search summary) lists countdown and expiring offers as pressure that pushes children into rash decisions, and the Children's Code Standard 13 (opened) says not to exploit unconscious psychological processes. Daily quests should roll over quietly, not expire with a red clock.
- Autoplay, infinite next-puzzle chains and hidden exits — Removes natural stopping points and works against the ICO's call to nudge toward breaks and give pause-and-save tools (opened). NN/g found children shrug off a failing site and move to alternatives, so a hidden exit does not retain them, it only annoys the parent. Always show a big Back/Home and a clear 'enough for today'.
- Ads, cross-promotion and cartoon characters that lead off-task — NN/g (opened): children can't distinguish ads from real content and click them more than adults, and they assume an ad with a cartoon character leads to a game. Keep the product ad-free, and keep external links behind the parent PIN.
- Red X, buzzer and 'wrong' language after a miss — The owner already forbids the word 'wrong'. Keep that for audio too: avoid sad or harsh sounds. Pair soft language with a concrete next step (Hattie and Timperley model, not opened) so the child never faces a dead end.
- Copy-pasted adult attention statistics and unverified learning myths in the product or the sales copy — I found no traceable primary source for 'age + N minutes' attention rules or the '8-second attention span' claim (search summaries). Quoting them to parents erodes trust. Use your own measured session data instead.

### Local context: Uzbekistan / Central Asia for a kids' (6-12) RU/UZ learning PWA on low-end Android

Verified by opening sources: (1) Uzbekistan's Latin alphabet is mid-reform. Lawmakers passed it in July 2026 and the Senate approved it on 10 Sept 2026. Oʻ, Gʻ, Sh, Ch become single letters Ö, Ğ, Ş, Ç, and "ng" stops being a separate letter. I found no confirmation that the president has signed, and no effective date. A deputy minister said that if it takes effect in 2027, grade-1 textbooks switch first and all textbooks by 2031 (Kursiv; Times of Central Asia). Davlatjon's Uzbek content is written in the old orthography (ʻ, U+02BB), so text should go through one script layer. (2) Android is about 82% of Uzbek mobile web traffic (StatCounter, Sept 2026; traffic, not device ownership). Internet use is about 89% and median mobile download speed is about 38 Mbps (DataReportal, early 2025). Connectivity is decent; the real costs are bytes, unstable 4G and cheap phones. (3) Parents: the edtech market is growing (children's segment +1,095% in 2024, Spot.uz). Telegram reaches more than 70% of the population and is the sales channel. Buyers distrust online learning and prefer state diplomas. Tutoring is widespread and a source of stress for children (Kun.uz, 2023). (4) Chess: a 2018 resolution put chess into the mandatory curriculum of 150 pilot schools. A 2021 state programme (reported by RFE/RL) obliged chess for grades 2-4, with an 18-hour course in 1,000 schools chosen by competition. I could NOT verify that chess is compulsory nationwide today. The programme ran to 2025 and I found no 2024-26 source, so do not claim "compulsory". (5) PWA: web.dev gives a 170 KB critical-path baseline (Moto G4, slow 3G, TTI under 5 s), a user-gesture install prompt via beforeinstallprompt, and warns that range requests for audio from a service worker need care. MDN confirms best-effort storage can be evicted. Measured in the live app: 536 mp3 files, 80 MB in total (median 139 KB, max 749 KB); sw.js:41 deliberately skips every .mp3, so no narration works offline; mp3 are served with Cache-Control max-age=0; the home page references 16 JS/CSS chunks, 1.72 MB raw and 495 KB gzip; no beforeinstallprompt handler and no navigator.storage.persist call exist in src; the "ʻ" glyph in Nunito is 0.5 em wide (16 px at 32 px), nearly as wide as "o", which gives the visible gap in "ko ʻr" and "oʻqib" in richuz-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg. What is good: normalizeText in checks.ts:47-53 already treats o', oʻ, o‘, o` as the same; the fresh-launch dialog offers a Русский / Oʻzbekcha switch at the top; Nunito ships cyrillic and latin-ext subsets (Ğ Ş are in the unicode-range), so the new letters load without a font swap. NOT verified (no usable source): RAM of typical family phones; mobile data price per GB; the share of children on a shared parent phone in Uzbekistan; home-language split in Tashkent versus regions; exact current child-data rules (only the 2021 data-localisation headline was confirmed, not the legal text). Items marked verified=false rest on search snippets or background knowledge.

- **Alphabet-proof Uzbek text layer (script switch)** (verified; https://uz.kursiv.media/en/2026-07-07/uzbekistan-lawmakers-approve-updates-to-latin-based-national-alphabet/ ; https://timesca.com/uzbekistan-latin-alphabet-changes-senate/) — One function converts canonical Uzbek strings between the current orthography (oʻ gʻ sh ch) and the proposed one (ö ğ ş ç). Strings are stored once in a single canonical form. Answer matching and search are normalised to a script-independent key. _Why:_ Both sources agree on the change: 26 letters plus 3 digraphs become 28 letters plus one apostrophe, with a staged transition (documents stay valid; grade-1 books first if the law applies from 2027; all textbooks by 2031, per a deputy minister). Senate approval is reported for 10 Sept 2026, but signature and effective date are unconfirmed. Children will meet both spellings (old books, new books) for years. Officials also say the reform fixes the >10 apostrophe variants that break search and software. The app has half of this already: normalizeText (src/lib/checks.ts:47-53) collapses apostrophe variants. _For Davlatjon:_ 1) Keep all Uzbek content in the current orthography with ʻ (src/lib/i18n.ts, src/content/meta.ts). Add a render-time helper toScript(text, 'current'|'new'), applied in the t(ru, uz) pair function in i18n.ts. 2) Add a parent setting "Alphabet: current / new", defaulting to current until the law is in force. 3) Extend normalizeText so ö/ğ/ş/ç and oʻ/gʻ/sh/ch give the same comparison key, so a child typing either way is right. 4) Never put Uzbek words inside images or SVG text (they cannot be switched). 5) Narration (ElevenLabs) is unaffected; the text under the Read-aloud button should follow the chosen script. 6) Add a unit test with words like ko'r, ogʻzaki, choy, shahar, tong. Careful: s'h and ng are ambiguous, so convert in one direction only (old to new) using a word list or explicit marks.
- **Fix the wide Uzbek ʻ (oʻ, gʻ) so words read as one word** (verified; Local measurement: Playwright canvas measureText on the live app; screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Davlatjon/7885c37e-ed41-5319-8669-624304e7892c/scratchpad/audit-tiles/richuz-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg) — In Nunito, U+02BB (ʻ) has an advance of 16 px at 32 px font size (0.5 em), about as wide as 'o' (18 px). U+02BC (ʼ) is 10 px and ASCII ' is 7 px. In the Uzbek screenshots this shows as a gap and a floating mark: "ko ʻr", "o ʻzingga", "Oʻ zbekcha". _Why:_ A first-grader decoding syllable by syllable reads "o ʻ zingga" as separate pieces. Aziz is the persona most hurt by this. The fix is purely typographic. _For Davlatjon:_ Wrap ʻ in a tiny inline span (class .tutuq) with negative side margins (about -0.15em left and -0.15em right) and slightly higher position. Do this in the same helper as the script switch, so it also covers the future ö ğ ş ç letters, which have no such problem. Check at 112% and 'bigText' size. Add a visual regression shot for oʻ, gʻ in a heading, a button and a task title.
- **Offline audio packs per day, instead of 80 MB of uncached on-demand mp3** (verified; https://web.dev/articles/sw-range-requests ; local files /home/user/Davlatjon/public/sw.js:41 and public/audio (536 files, 80 MB)) — Let a parent (or the child, with a Wi-Fi hint) download "today's sounds" or a whole week into the Cache API. The service worker then serves them cache-first. web.dev notes that a cached audio response must answer Range requests correctly (browsers ask for audio in slices). It calls writing that slicing code by hand non-trivial and points to Workbox's range-requests plugin. _Why:_ Today sw.js skips every .mp3 ("browser requests sound in chunks, so we do not cache it"), so narration (the key support for Aziz) always needs the network, even for a clip heard yesterday. The files are served with Cache-Control: max-age=0, so each play costs at least a revalidation round trip. The median clip is about 139 KB, but long ones reach 749 KB (secret-sages.mp3, w2d7r.mp3). A weekly pack of Uzbek or Russian task audio is a few MB, well within reach of a one-off Wi-Fi download. _For Davlatjon:_ 1) Make audio files immutable and versioned (a hash in the name, Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable). 2) In sw.js add a cacheFirst route for /audio/ that handles Range (use Workbox RangeRequestsPlugin, or fetch the whole file and slice from cache). Cache only the language the child uses. 3) On /parent add "Download sounds for offline: Week 1 (X MB)" with a progress bar and a size shown before download. 4) Preload only the single clip for the open task (preload=metadata, never auto-play). 5) Use navigator.storage.estimate() to avoid filling a cheap phone.
- **Hold a hard performance budget based on a cheap Android, not on a dev laptop** (verified; https://web.dev/articles/performance-budgets-101 ; https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2025-uzbekistan ; https://gs.statcounter.com/os-market-share/mobile/uzbekistan) — web.dev's baseline is under 170 KB of critical-path resources, with Time to Interactive under 5 s on a Moto G4 over slow 3G, enforced in CI. Uzbek context: Android is 82.28% of mobile web traffic (StatCounter, Sept 2026); median mobile download is 37.8 Mbps (Ookla via DataReportal, early 2025). So the average connection is decent, but cheap phones and variable 4G are the constraint, not 2G. _Why:_ Measured on the live app: the home HTML references 16 JS/CSS chunks, 1.72 MB raw and 495 KB gzip (curl), about 3x the 170 KB web.dev baseline, although not all of it is on the critical path. Page height is 9.1 viewports on phone / (audit-metrics.json). A $100-ish phone (import average about $102-116 per unit in 2025 customs statistics, from a search snippet, not opened) parses JS slowly, which Aziz sees as a frozen button after a tap. _For Davlatjon:_ 1) Add a CI budget (size-limit or Lighthouse CI): home route JS at most 170 KB gzip, each task route a similar cap. 2) Load chess-only code (chess engine, 572 KB of puzzle JSON in public/puzzles, the board) only on /chess routes with dynamic import; fetch a theme's puzzle file only when that theme is opened. 3) Test with Chrome DevTools 4x CPU slowdown plus Slow 4G, and measure INP on the first tap in a task. 4) Show a skeleton and a 'big button' immediately (no layout shift) before heavy tools load.
- **A parent-gesture install prompt at a moment of success** (verified; https://web.dev/articles/customize-install) — Capture the beforeinstallprompt event, call preventDefault() to suppress the mini-infobar, keep the event, and show your own "Add to home screen" button; call prompt() only from a tap, then read userChoice. prompt() can be called once per saved event. Listen for appinstalled to hide the offer. web.dev says to consider how users typically use the PWA before promoting it. The page does not cover iOS. _Why:_ A home-screen icon lets a 7-year-old start without a browser, a typed URL or a Google search. grep of /home/user/Davlatjon/src finds no beforeinstallprompt handler, so Android Chrome's generic prompt is the only route. manifest.ts says "от 7 лет" (product is 6-12) and has lang "ru" only. _For Davlatjon:_ Show a small card on /parent and after the first completed daily quest: "Put Davlatjon on the phone screen" with a big icon, in the UI language, with a voiced line. For iOS Safari, show a 3-step picture guide (Share, Add to Home Screen) because there is no event. Never show it on the child's first launch or in the middle of a task. Fix manifest: description 6-12 and, if possible, an Uzbek manifest variant.
- **Protect local progress: persistent storage plus a portable backup** (verified; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage_API/Storage_quotas_and_eviction_criteria ; grep of src (no storage.persist)) — Request navigator.storage.persist(). MDN: best-effort storage is evicted under storage pressure (least recently used first); on Safari with tracking prevention, script-written data is deleted after 7 days without interaction; localStorage is capped at 5 MiB per origin. Persistent data is removed only by the user. _Why:_ All progress lives in localStorage key davlatjon-lab:v1; no persist() call exists in src. Cheap phones with full storage are common, and parents clean browser data. Losing a child's 3-week streak, certificates and crowns is the most emotionally damaging failure and breaks trust in the "parent area". _For Davlatjon:_ Call persist() after the first reward and when installed. Add on /parent a "Save progress" action: export a short text code or a file (also a QR) and a "Restore" box. Warn in plain words before the parent clears data. Keep the optional Google/Telegram sync as a second route. Show "Saved on this phone only" in /parent.
- **Light-weight profiles for siblings on one family phone** (unverified; background knowledge; indirect evidence from search snippets on shared-device access in India (Central Square Foundation BaSE 2025 factsheets) and Nigeria/Rwanda smartphone trials, none opened) — Allow 2-4 child profiles on one device: avatar plus first name plus age, no passwords for children, a one-tap "Who is playing?" screen at launch, and a separate progress record per child (still local). _Why:_ Household phones are shared in many low-income settings; the evidence I found is from India and Africa, not Uzbekistan, and I found no Uzbek statistic on children's shared use. The brief says "one profile per device" and also names Aziz (7) and Dilnoza (10) as users of a parent's phone; two siblings in one family would overwrite each other's streak, age-adapted tasks and rank. _For Davlatjon:_ Treat the profile as an array in davlatjon-lab:v1 (migration: one existing profile becomes the first). Home shows big avatar buttons; the parent PIN area manages them and lets a parent merge or delete. Rank, quest and hint settings follow the profile (age drives difficulty). Add pass-and-play chess (two kids on one phone) as a cheap competition mode for Dilnoza.
- **Telegram-native sharing for parents, not email or accounts** (verified; https://www.spot.uz/ru/2025/07/01/edtech-rise/) — Spot.uz reports that over 70% of the population uses Telegram and that edtech courses are often sold through known bloggers, because buyers trust familiar faces more than unknown brands. Local edtech also faces distrust of online learning, preference for state diplomas, weak digital skills and low purchasing power. _Why:_ The household's communication channel is already Telegram. A parent will react to a message in the family chat faster than to an app notification, and a child can show a friend a certificate there (Dilnoza's goal). It needs no server or login: Web Share API or a t.me share link opens the Telegram chooser. _For Davlatjon:_ 1) Add a "Send to Mum/Dad" button on completed days and on certificates, which shares a generated image (canvas) plus one line: "Anna finished week 1, 18 tasks, 4 days". 2) A weekly parent summary card (picture, not a table) that is also shareable. 3) Keep the name optional on shared images: nickname or first name only, chosen by the parent. 4) For the optional Telegram sync, make sure the bot never writes to the child directly.
- **Earn parent trust: calm, short, school-compatible, no test pressure** (verified; https://www.kun.uz/kr/news/2023/11/08/bolaga-stress-va-tabaqalanish-xavfi-nega-repetitorga-borish-shart-bolib-qoldi ; https://www.uzdaily.uz/en/uzbek-parents-increase-spending-on-school-and-digital-tools/ ; https://www.spot.uz/ru/2025/07/01/edtech-rise/) — Kun.uz (2023, interviews and opinion, partly unsourced) says that entry to universities is by test, that tutoring has become almost essential, and that it can add stress and status pressure on children. UzDaily (19 Aug 2026, Wildberries Research Center survey) reports that 55% of parents plan or consider educational subscriptions or tutoring; 70% of those pick tutoring; price and discounts come first when choosing, then the child's taste. Spot.uz notes preference for state diplomas and distrust of online learning. _Why:_ The parent is a stressed buyer comparing the app with a tutor. The strongest differentiator is the opposite of a tutor: 10-15 calm minutes, a visible reason to trust (clear curriculum, no ads, no data sale), and a child who asks to play. The Kun.uz claim that extra courses cause depression is not backed by cited studies in the article, so I only use it as a sign of parental worry. _For Davlatjon:_ 1) On /parent show "Today: 12 minutes, 3 quests done" and a plain sentence about what the child practised this week (skills, not scores). 2) Put a visible "daily time limit / end of session" screen ("Great! Enough for today") which supports the 'short safe sessions' wish. 3) Offer a printable certificate (already built) worded as the app's own certificate, never as official school documents. 4) Add a short "What is inside" parent page: no ads, no chat, no purchases, data stays on the phone. 5) Do not add test-prep framing, percentile ranks or comparison with other children.
- **School-chess alignment, stated honestly** (verified; https://www.uzdaily.uz/en/chess-lessons-to-be-introduced-in-uzbek-schools/ ; https://anhor.uz/society/v-150-shkolah-uzbekistana-poyavyatsya-uroki-shahmat/ ; https://www.currenttime.tv/a/uzbek-schools-teaching-chess/31049088.html) — What I could confirm: (a) 2018, a presidential resolution put pilot chess lessons into the mandatory curriculum of 150 general schools (UzDaily, Anhor), with a plan to extend stage by stage. (b) 2021, a state programme (RFE/RL) obliged teaching chess in grades 2-4; in-depth teaching in 150 schools from 2021/22 within physical-education lessons; an 18-hour chess curriculum in 1,000 schools selected by competition. (c) The FIDE page on the January 2021 decree only mentions elementary school and a "Chess in school" project, and does not say compulsory. NOT verified: whether chess is compulsory in all schools in 2026. The programme ran to 2025 and I found no 2024-2026 source. _Why:_ The statement 'chess is a compulsory subject in some Uzbek schools' holds for the pilot schools and, per one secondary source, for grades 2-4. Parents of children who study chess at school look for homework help and a place to practise between lessons. The 18-hour course shape (a short course) is a sign that lessons are short and basic. _For Davlatjon:_ 1) Do not write "compulsory in all schools" anywhere in the UI or marketing. 2) Offer a parent-side line: "Many schools teach chess in grades 2-4; ask your school teacher which topics this term" and a topic list that mirrors the early levels (board, pieces, moves, mate in 1). 3) Use the Uzbek terms the school teachers actually use for pieces (check with a teacher or the school textbook before recording more audio). 4) Add a short 'before the school chess lesson' drill (3 minutes). 5) Add pass-and-play chess for school friends.
- **Language-first, voiced, one-question-per-screen onboarding for RU/UZ** (unverified; Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Davlatjon/7885c37e-ed41-5319-8669-624304e7892c/scratchpad/audit-tiles/fresh-phone-home-t1.jpg ; background knowledge for language statistics (census figures from a search snippet, not opened)) — First screen: two big buttons showing each language in its own name (Русский, Oʻzbekcha) with a speaker, then name, then age, each on its own screen. Language can be switched at any time from the header. Uzbek is the mother tongue of most residents (about 91% per a 2026 census snippet) and Russian is widely understood in cities (about 7 million speakers per a 2025 estimate, method not stated), and about 10% of schools teach in Russian (PM statement, 2023, per a snippet). All three figures are unverified here. _Why:_ The fresh-launch dialog (fresh-phone-home-t1.jpg) already has a language switch, which is good, but it sits in the top corner at about 36 CSS px high, above a block of text with three rules before the name field (name input at about y=708 CSS px of an 839 px viewport). A first-grader meets a wall of text. A parent who opens it first may choose a language the child does not read best. _For Davlatjon:_ 1) Make the language step its own screen with two 64 px buttons. Remember the choice and set <html lang> (it is already set to uz at runtime in layout.tsx). 2) Voice the three rules (a greeting button exists), and show them as three icon cards after the name and age, not before. 3) Name the language in its own language and avoid flags. 4) Let a bilingual child flip a single task to the other language without changing the whole UI. 5) Keep Uzbek Latin only, but note that older relatives and some media (Kun.uz has a /kr/ Cyrillic edition) still use Cyrillic Uzbek; do not add it now.
- **Child-data caution for optional Google/Telegram sync (data localisation)** (unverified; https://kun.uz/en/news/2021/01/26/personal-data-of-uzbek-citizens-are-now-required-to-be-stored-in-uzbekistan (headline only readable); search snippets from Mondaq and DataGuidance) — A January 2021 amendment to the Law on Personal Data, per search summaries, requires operators to collect and store Uzbek citizens' personal data on servers located in Uzbekistan, registered in a state register. The Kun.uz page only showed its headline when I opened it, so I could not verify details, scope or penalties. I found nothing on how it applies to children. _Why:_ Davlatjon asks for a name and age, and optionally syncs progress through Google or Telegram. Local-first storage is the safest default and a selling point to parents. If the sync stores a child's name on a foreign server, the legal position needs a lawyer. _For Davlatjon:_ Keep local-first as the default and advertise it. For sync: store only a nickname and numeric progress, make sync opt-in by the parent in /parent, show a plain-language notice of what leaves the phone and where it is stored, and get local legal advice on the 2021 rule before launch. This is not legal advice.
- **Competition without ranking children: personal bests and team goals** (unverified; background knowledge; local context in https://www.kun.uz/kr/news/2023/11/08/bolaga-stress-va-tabaqalanish-xavfi-nega-repetitorga-borish-shart-bolib-qoldi (stress from comparison, opinion article)) — Give Dilnoza challenge and something to show friends without a public leaderboard: beat-your-own-best, a weekly family goal, and shareable badges that show effort (days played, puzzles solved) instead of rating. _Why:_ The owner's principles already hide ratings under 10. In a market where comparison and status through tutoring are noted by Kun.uz, a public ranking would pull the product towards the pressure parents are trying to escape. Personal-best and 'family goal' keep the competitive streak of a 10-year-old but reward effort. _For Davlatjon:_ Chess: robot level crowns and personal-best puzzle streak stay. Add a 'family week' goal that fills when any child on the phone plays (works with sibling profiles). For friends: a challenge code that gives the same 5 puzzles, with results shown as 'solved N of 5' without a number rating.

Anti-patterns:

- Hard-coding Uzbek spellings (and baking Uzbek text into images) — The Latin alphabet is changing (Senate approval reported 10 Sept 2026; staged transition through about 2031). Text inside PNG/SVG, scattered string literals and audio scripts cannot be switched. Children would see one spelling at school and another in the app.
- Auto-downloading or auto-playing audio on mobile data — The audio library is 80 MB across 536 files. Pre-fetching it on a family's metered 4G, on a phone with little storage, is costly and easy to blame on the app. Download only on a parent's action, with the size shown.
- Silent reliance on localStorage for everything the child has earned — MDN confirms best-effort storage can be evicted under pressure, and Safari clears script data after 7 days without interaction. A lost streak, certificate or crown on a shared phone feels like punishment and destroys trust.
- Test-prep and tutor-style pressure (percentiles, 'be #1', score pages for parents) — Parents are already under pressure from test-based admission and tutoring (Kun.uz). Ranking children against each other adds stress and conflicts with the owner's no-rating-numbers-under-10 principle.
- Loss-aversion streaks, guilt copy, and push notifications aimed at the child — 'Don't lose your streak' and sad-mascot messages are manipulative for 6-12 year olds. A gentle streak and a parent-side reminder are fine; child-side nagging is not.
- Forcing an account, phone number or Telegram login to start — It adds a barrier for Aziz's parent, collects child data that may fall under localisation rules (unverified scope), and breaks the local-first promise. Keep login optional and parent-side.
- Ads, rewarded-ad hints, loot-box style random rewards or in-app purchases visible to children — They exploit children's limited impulse control, interrupt thinking and contradict the 'hints open one by one' principle. Uzbek law on protecting children from harmful information (2017) also sets age-labelling expectations for content.
- Marketing claims that cannot be verified (e.g. 'chess is compulsory in schools', 'approved by the ministry') — Only the 2018 pilot (150 schools) and a 2021 programme for grades 2-4 are confirmed; the current national status is not. A false claim costs trust with exactly the careful parents the product wants.
- Machine-translated or mixed-script Uzbek, or Russian-only voice with an Uzbek interface — Awkward Uzbek reads as foreign to children and parents, and mismatched audio and text confuse early readers. Keep human-written pairs and recorded narration in the language shown.

### kidsux: UX and accessibility guidance for children 6-12, applied to Davlatjon

What I opened and read: NN/g articles on kids' cognition, physical development and usability issues; W3C WCAG 2.2 Understanding pages (2.5.8, 2.5.5, 2.2.2, 2.3.3, 2.5.7); ICO Children's Code standards 5 and 13; the FTC COPPA FAQ; the Radesky 2022 JAMA Netw Open paper (PMC); Wery and Diliberto 2017 (PMC); the Sesame Workshop 2012 report's landing page at the Cooney Center. Not opened, so marked unverified: the full Anthony 2019 MTAGIC PDF (only the abstract; no child target-size numbers), the Hiniker 2016 PDF, the Deci 1999 PDF, the BDA style guide, Apple HIG and Material pages (the fetches returned no body text), the FTC ABCmouse page (404), and every competitor platform. The NN/g age-band guidance is mostly for ages 3-12 and is dated, and NN/g itself says even a few years change what children can do. Most of it fits 6-12 only loosely. Do not read it as a 6-12 spec.

Audit evidence from the app. Good things first. (1) The wrong-answer path is soft. Typing 5 for 19+19+19 gave "Давай проверим твою идею! Какая часть решения точно верная?" (my probe, scratchpad/audit-agents/kidsux/wrong.png), with no word "wrong". (2) The chess board squares are about 117 px in the 1082 px tile, which is about 44.5 CSS px (kid7-phone-game-robot-t1.jpg), so they just meet the AAA 44 px size. (3) The numeric field has inputmode=numeric. (4) The main CTAs ("Начать", "Продолжить") are big orange buttons with a clear shadow. (5) html lang="ru" is set, body text is 16 px with 24 px line height, and a prefers-reduced-motion rule exists (1 rule against 5 keyframes). (6) The welcome dialog has a "Послушать приветствие" button.

Problems measured or seen, in order of weight for Aziz (7). A. The header nav is icon-only and small: knight 36x34, pencil 42x34, lock 42x34, logo 129x40 (smallSamples for "phone /", repeated on every page). That is below 44, and at the Pixel 7 density (about 158 CSS ppi, my calculation) 36 px is about 5.8 mm. B. The day task tabs are 40x40 emoji-only squares. Two of them are the same icon (🔢, 🔢), and the strip is cut off on the right (rich-phone-day1-t1, fresh-phone-day1-t1-t1). C. The soft feedback card renders below the "Проверить" button, half hidden behind the sticky "Начало 1/8 Дальше" bar (wrong.png). A child who tapped the button and sees nothing has to scroll. No sound or character accompanies it. D. /chess/history is a mobile bug the metrics missed. documentElement.scrollWidth is 869 against clientWidth 412 (my Playwright probe). The screenshot is 2281 px wide and content fills only the left half (rich-phone-history-t2.jpg), although the metrics file says hOverflow=false. The page also has 133 targets under 44 px, 120 under 32 px, 402 text nodes under 14 px, and a ratio of 13.5 screens. E. Text density. The welcome dialog opens with three rules of text (fresh-phone-home-t1.jpg), and the chess hub opens with a 5-line paragraph (kid7-phone-chess-t1.jpg). The home hero headline "Математика — это место, где происходят интересные вещи" takes 4 lines and says nothing concrete for a child (kid7-phone-home-t1.jpg). The "Read aloud" pill is about 36 CSS px tall. F. Home page length: ratio 9.1, 38 interactive elements, 63 text nodes under 14 px. /chess is 7.5 screens with 73 small text nodes. G. Accessible names: /chess has 16 unnamed interactive elements, /chess/puzzles 16, /chess/openings 554, /chess/games 196, /chess/endgames 54, /chess/play#robot-2-w 32. These are probably board squares or cards, so check before treating them as a defect. They matter if you rely on screen readers or switch access. H. "Звёзд дня: 0." is shown in rich-phone-home-t3.jpg (a zero-count text style). The fire icon with "3 дня подряд" is gentle, but the flame metaphor will turn into loss framing once a streak breaks. Check what the UI says on day 4 of a missed streak.

Order of work I would propose for phase 4: (1) fix the /chess/history overflow, (2) enlarge the nav and tabs and label them, (3) make feedback visible and audible, (4) cut text on the first screens and promote "Read aloud", (5) the "stop here" session closure.

- **Audio plus visual instruction as the default for under-9s, not an optional button** (verified; https://joanganzcooneycenter.org/?p=19607 and https://www.nngroup.com/articles/kids-cognition/) — Sesame Workshop's 2012 report (page says it rests on 50+ studies of preschoolers) recommends spoken dialogue plus visual cues for children who cannot read yet. NN/g reports that combined audio and visual instructions worked, and that children skip long instructional text. _Why:_ Slow decoding eats working memory, which NN/g notes is smaller in children than adults. Voice moves the instruction off the reading channel so the child's attention goes to the task. Caveat: both sources are about 3-8 year-olds. A claim that narration should finish before controls unlock came only from a secondary summary of Sesame's report and I could not confirm it on the page, so do not copy that rule. _For Davlatjon:_ For age 6-8 (the 'Режим занятий: 6–8 лет' mode already exists), make the 'Прочитать' button the first, largest control on every task and lesson: a 56+ px pill with a speaker icon at the top of the card, not the 36 px pill beside 'Задача 1 из 8' (kid7-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg). Show it with a sound-wave that moves while playing and a stop toggle. Keep it tap-to-play, no auto-play, because auto-play on a shared parent phone surprises people. Highlight the sentence being read if the clip timing allows. Put a speaker button on the welcome dialog's three rules as the first element, not after them (fresh-phone-home-t1.jpg).
- **Big targets by age, with the hit area larger than the drawing** (verified; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/children-ux-physical-development/ and https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html and https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced.html) — NN/g: 2 cm x 2 cm touch targets for ages 3-5 (about 4 times the adult 1 cm), same advice for under 9 on touch, adult sizes by about 11. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA): at least 24x24 CSS px, with spacing and inline exceptions. SC 2.5.5 (AAA): 44x44. NN/g gives no separate size for 9-12. _Why:_ Fine motor control is limited until about 9, so a small target means a missed tap, then a repeated tap, then a frustrated child. My calculation for a Pixel 7: about 158 CSS ppi, so 1 cm is about 62 CSS px and NN/g's 2 cm is about 125 CSS px. That is not realistic for every control, so use it for primary actions only. The Anthony 2019 MTAGIC review (6 studies, 116 children) reports that children acquire touch targets less accurately than adults, but I could not read its numeric recommendations. _For Davlatjon:_ Set a token such as --tap-min: 48px for all ages, 56-64px for age<10 on primary actions (Проверить, Дальше, Начать, Прочитать, hint). Fix the measured offenders: header knight 36x34, pencil 42x34, lock 42x34, day tabs 40x40, back arrow 40x40, print 45x36 (smallSamples in audit-metrics.json). Add padding or ::after to extend the hit area without changing the picture. Also fix /chess/play (37 small targets), /chess/secrets (41), /chess/history (133, 120 under 32 px). Keep at least 8 px between neighbours. Chess board squares at about 44.5 px are acceptable; do not shrink the board below 8 x 44 px.
- **Every drag has a tap equivalent** (verified; https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html and https://www.nngroup.com/articles/children-ux-physical-development/) — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 (AA): everything done with a dragging movement must also be possible with a single pointer without dragging. NN/g: precise dragging is hard for young children, so let them do the same action by dragging or by tapping a destination; dragging with a mouse is mastered around 9-11. _Why:_ Dragging needs the finger to stay on the glass and a steady path, which is exactly what small hands on a moving 4G phone do badly. Tap-source then tap-destination also works for a switch user and for Aziz's parent's cracked screen. _For Davlatjon:_ Hanoi, balance scales, river crossing, the robot programmer and number machines should all support select-then-place. Chess already works this way if click-click moves are supported (test: tap the e2 pawn, then e4 on the 412 px board). Show the selected piece with a ring and show legal targets as dots. Never require a drag in exercises under age 9. If a drag exists, snap generously (accept a drop within about 1 square) and never penalise a missed drop.
- **Icon plus word, and no two controls with the same picture** (verified; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/kids-cognition/) — NN/g saw a 7-year-old ask 'What does this "2" mean? It's annoying!' about an unlabelled number, and young children not understanding undo/redo buttons. Hiniker et al. 2016 (IJHCS 90:53-67, 34 preschoolers 2-5, abstract seen only via search) found informal symbols such as symbolic progress bars largely unusable for the youngest. I could not open the paper, so use it only as a hint that symbols are not self-explanatory. _Why:_ Emoji look universal to adults but a child assigns the nearest literal meaning. A label gives a second route: the word, or the audio when tapped. For Aziz the word is also reading practice. _For Davlatjon:_ The day-task tab strip has two identical 🔢 tabs and nine emoji-only squares (rich-phone-day1-t1, fresh-phone-day1-t1-t1). Give each tab a one-word caption under the icon or, better, replace the strip by the 'Задача 1 из 8' stepper with dots. Header: add visible labels under icons for age<10 ('Шахматы', 'Мои задачи', 'Родителям'); the accessible names already exist (smallSamples show '♞Шахматы'), so this is a CSS change. Keep 🔒 as the parent marker but add the word. In Uzbek, check that labels fit at 412 px (richuz-phone-home).
- **One screen, one idea, short text, text-level matching the child** (verified; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/childrens-websites-usability-issues/) — NN/g: children skipped long paragraphs of instructions (Study 2 on a mint kids site, Study 3 on Roblox), reading goes from none to tentative to scanning by age, and they react negatively to text one grade above or below their own. NN/g separates young (3-5), mid (6-8) and older (9-12) children. Their Teen report advises a 6th-grade level for broad audiences; that is teen guidance, not 6-12. _Why:_ Skimming kids act on what is visible. A short line plus a picture gets used; a paragraph does not. Aziz's 10 minutes of attention is better spent on tasks than decoding framing text. _For Davlatjon:_ Cut first-screen text. Examples: the welcome dialog's three rules become three icon cards with one word each ('Не торопись', 'Подсказка', 'Объясни') plus audio; the chess hub paragraph 'Каждый уровень — это урок, правила, словарик…' (kid7-phone-chess-t1.jpg) becomes one line; the home hero line becomes 'Привет, Анна! Продолжим?' with the day title below. Keep task statements under about 20 words for age 6-8, and move 'Сначала посчитай так, как тебе удобно. А потом…' into a second step revealed after the first answer. Use the existing age setting to pick text variants in the content files (age-adapted tasks already exist). Check Uzbek for length: Uzbek strings run longer (richuz-phone-play-t1 uses a 4-line intro).
- **Readable type: larger sizes, generous spacing; skip 'dyslexia fonts'** (verified; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5629233/ and https://www.nngroup.com/articles/childrens-websites-usability-issues/) — NN/g's 14 pt for young children vs 12 pt for older children and adults (about 18.7 vs 16 CSS px, my conversion). Wery and Diliberto 2017 (12 elementary students with dyslexia, alternating-treatment design): OpenDyslexic gave no gain in rate or accuracy, effect sizes were negative against Arial and Times New Roman, and no child preferred it. The study is small. Dyslexia-association guides (BDA-derived summaries, which I did not open on the BDA site) suggest 12-14 pt, 1.5 line spacing and left alignment; one charity notes there is no consistent advantage of sans serif over serif and that spacing matters more than letter shape. _Why:_ Spacing and size lower crowding for every beginner reader, not only children with a diagnosis. Nunito Variable (the current font) is a rounded sans with clear letterforms; line height 24 px on 16 px text is 1.5 already. _For Davlatjon:_ Raise base text to 18 px for age 6-8 (a 'bigText' setting exists; make it the default for age<9 instead of a switch buried in settings). Cut sub-14 px text: the home page has 63 such text nodes, /chess has 73, /chess/history has 402. Keep captions at 14 px minimum. Left-align everything, no justified text. Add a parent-visible 'Spacing' toggle (letter and word spacing +10-15 percent) rather than a special font. Check that Cyrillic and Uzbek Latin diacritics (o‘, g‘) keep their marks readable at 18 px.
- **Visible, adjacent, multi-channel soft feedback** (verified; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/kids-cognition/) — NN/g: children under 6 missed subtle character reactions and understood feedback better when expressions were exaggerated or said aloud; around 6 they began to read subtle cues, but cultural differences in sounds can block meaning. Instructions in audio plus visual worked. _Why:_ A child who taps 'Проверить' and sees nothing happen concludes the app is broken or ignores it. The message has to appear where the eyes are and use more than one channel. _For Davlatjon:_ Keep the owner's wording ('Давай проверим твою идею!'), it is good. Fix delivery: in wrong.png the amber card appears below the button and is half under the sticky nav bar. Scroll the card into view, make it the same width as the answer box, add aria-live=polite, give the robot mascot a short head tilt (with reduced-motion fallback) and a 1-second chime that is clearly neutral (not a buzzer). For a correct answer, make the reaction bigger and consistent: a star, a short voice clip, a soft confetti. Read the feedback line aloud for age<9 only if the child has sound on. Never use red alone; add the icon.
- **One obvious next step per screen; no redundant navigation** (verified; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/childrens-websites-usability-issues/) — NN/g: multiple or redundant navigation is very confusing for children, young children avoid scrolling, and older children scroll when cues show more content. Young children did not use Back; when stuck they refreshed, reopened, then left. _Why:_ A child decides in seconds. If three equal choices compete, the child picks the loudest or leaves. A stuck child needs an exit that does not need Back. _For Davlatjon:_ Home is 9.1 screens long with 38 interactive elements (phone /). For age<10, show a short home: greeting, ONE big 'Продолжить' (next math day or next chess exercise), the daily quest of 3 as three big checkboxes, then 'Ещё' for everything else (weeks list, awards, openings). Chess hub is 7.5 screens (phone /chess); same treatment: next lesson first, secondary tools (history, endgames, review, openings) under 'Ещё'. Add a persistent 'Домой' control on game screens, since young children do not use Back. Stick with the current day page pattern (1/8, Дальше) which is clear.
- **Built-in stopping points and a pause the child controls** (verified; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/childrens-information/childrens-code-guidance-and-resources/age-appropriate-design-a-code-of-practice-for-online-services/5-detrimental-use-of-data/) — ICO Children's Code standard 5 lists reward loops, continuous scrolling, notifications and auto-play as engagement-extending tactics, cites the UK Chief Medical Officers' precautionary advice, and recommends neutral options to keep going (no implication of loss on stopping), no autoplay, and pause mechanisms 'which allow children to take a break at any time'. It does not name streaks. It is UK law, not binding in Uzbekistan, but a recognised benchmark. NN/g notes limited planning ability makes children vulnerable to game addiction and cites Baby Bus time limits as a model. _Why:_ Aziz has about 10 minutes of attention; a clear end gives a feeling of completion and keeps the parent's trust ('short safe sessions'). _For Davlatjon:_ After the daily quest of 3 is done, show a calm 'На сегодня достаточно' card with the star, the next-day teaser and a 'Ещё одну?' button of equal size to 'Закончить'. Do not auto-start the next task or the next puzzle. In puzzles/Woodpecker, add a pause button that hides the board timer and stops it. Offer the parent a session length (10/15/20 min) in /parent; at the limit, finish the current task and show the rest card instead of a hard cutoff. Keep the gentle streak but state it as 'You came 3 days' and never as 'Don't lose your streak'.
- **Motion that can be stopped and a quiet mode** (verified; https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html and https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html) — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 (A): moving, blinking or scrolling content that starts automatically, lasts over 5 seconds and sits beside other content needs pause/stop/hide. SC 2.3.3 (AAA): motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled unless essential, with the prefers-reduced-motion media query as the sufficient technique. NN/g adds that children like animation and sound more than adults do, so the target is control, not removal. _Why:_ Some children (ADHD, sensory sensitivity, vestibular issues) are overwhelmed by constant motion, and moving decoration competes with the task for attention. _For Davlatjon:_ The app has one prefers-reduced-motion rule and 5 keyframes (my probe), which is a good base. Check each loop that runs longer than 5 seconds (mascot idle, flame, progress shimmer, hero decoration). Add a 'Тихий режим' switch in parent settings that turns off decorative loops and confetti and keeps essential animation (a piece sliding to its square, the robot moving). Make celebration animations short (about 1.5 s) and non-looping. No flashing content.
- **Reward progress and effort, keep extrinsic payments small and informative** (unverified; Deci, Koestner and Ryan (1999), Psychological Bulletin 125:627-668 (seen only through search summaries)) — A meta-analysis of 128 experiments reported by search summaries: rewards given for engagement, completion or performance reduced later free-choice interest, tangible rewards were more harmful for children than for college students, and positive verbal feedback increased interest. The finding is contested: Cameron and Pierce (1994) found little harm, and Eisenberger et al. published a reply in the same journal. I did not read the PDF, so effect sizes are not quoted here. _Why:_ The idea is that rewards perceived as controlling shift the reason for doing something from curiosity to payment. For a thinking-skills product, curiosity is the product. _For Davlatjon:_ Keep XP, daily quest and certificates, but make rewards informational and not paid per click: stars for finishing the 3 things, a certificate for a real milestone (rank), and verbal feedback on strategy ('Ты проверил(а) оба случая') rather than points per answer. Do not attach XP to speed or time spent. Put 'what I learned today' in the end-of-session card. For Dilnoza (10, competitive), let her compare against her own past, not a leaderboard of other children.
- **Parent gate, data minimisation and parent-side sync** (verified; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions) — COPPA FAQ (first 100,000 characters read): applies to services directed to children under 13; verifiable parental consent before collecting personal information; persistent identifiers, voice/image recordings and geolocation count as personal information; operators cannot require more information than reasonably necessary and must delete data when no longer needed. The Rule was amended on 22 April 2025, so check current text. COPPA is US law; Uzbekistan has its own data law that I did not check. The ICO code's standard 13 (opened) also says nudges must not push children to give unnecessary data or switch off privacy, with high-privacy defaults for ages 0-9. _Why:_ A 6-12 year-old cannot consent to data sharing, and parents judge safety by what the first screen asks for. _For Davlatjon:_ Progress is local in localStorage, which is the right default. Keep Google/Telegram sync as a parent-only action behind the PIN, off by default, with a plain statement of what is sent. Child-facing screens should never show a sign-in button. The first-run asks for name and age (fresh-phone-home-t1): say why ('чтобы подобрать задачи'), allow a nickname instead of a real name (the text already says parents can change it), and do not request a surname. Make the 🔒 gate hard to pass by luck: PIN is fine; do not show the PIN hint to the child. Keep the 🔒 icon, add the word 'Родителям', and make it 48 px.
- **Do not rely on colour alone; check contrast and colour-blind pairs** (unverified; background knowledge) — About 1 in 12 boys have red-green colour deficiency (figure from memory, not checked). WCAG 1.4.1 and 1.4.3 (not opened for this audit) ask for non-colour cues and contrast ratios of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and UI components. _Why:_ Chess boards and state pills often use colour alone for 'correct', 'selected', 'last move' or 'hint', and a sound-and-shape cue keeps working for a child who sees those colours alike. _For Davlatjon:_ Check: the disabled 'Проверить' button is pale lavender with white text and likely under 3:1 (kid7-phone-day1-t1-t1.jpg); the chess board's tan and brown squares need highlight shapes (ring, dot) for 'selected' and 'legal move', not just tint (kid7-phone-game-robot-t1.jpg); '🟢 Комфортно' already pairs colour with a word, which is good. Run the pages through a colour-blindness simulator in Playwright (CSS filter or Chrome DevTools emulation) before changing colours.
- **Undo instead of confirm dialogs, and reversible mistakes** (verified; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/kids-cognition/) — NN/g: young children did not know what redo/undo buttons did and fell back on familiar tools such as an eraser; older children who understood redo still used the eraser. The practical reading: children understand 'take it back' when it looks and acts like what they know, and confirm dialogs ('Are you sure?') are a poor fit for them because they read neither the question nor the consequence. That second half is my inference, not a finding. _Why:_ A child who may undo a move with one tap needs no warning dialog. Dialogs also hide the action behind another tap and more reading. _For Davlatjon:_ The robot game already has a labelled '↶ Отменить' (kid7-phone-game-robot-t1.jpg, bottom), which is good. Extend: no 'Are you sure?' on any child-side action; use undo for chess moves and tool resets, and a 'Начать заново' that keeps the previous attempt for 5 seconds. Put destructive things (reset progress, delete profile, sync off) only in /parent, behind the PIN, with a typed or long-press confirm there. Label undo with an eraser or back-arrow icon plus the word.

Anti-patterns:

- Parasocial pressure and confirmshaming by the mascot — Radesky et al. 2022 (JAMA Netw Open, 133 apps used by 160 children aged 3-5; opened) found manipulative design in about 80% of apps (107 of 133) and nearly all children (98.8%) used at least one such app. Their example: a talking character asking 'Do you want to give up?' when the player stops. Davlatjon has a robot mascot and chess robots with lines like 'Иго-го! Я Конь…'; keep the characters encouraging and never sad, angry or disappointed when the child stops, loses or leaves. Evidence is from ages 3-5, not 6-12, but the mechanism (children trust characters) holds for 6-8.
- Fake urgency, countdowns and 'limited time' offers — Same Radesky 2022 study lists fabricated time pressure (countdown clocks, 'Limited time only!'). Daily quest and streak must never create artificial deadlines such as 'only 2 hours left'. Real time in Storm/Woodpecker modes is a game rule and can stay, but show it as an optional mode with pause and hide-the-clock option, and do not use red or flashing for the last seconds with under-10s (that last point is my judgement, not a cited finding).
- Loss-framed streaks and reward loops — ICO standard 5 (opened) names reward loops as an engagement-extending tactic and asks that options to keep going are presented neutrally, without implying the child will lose out by stopping. It does not name streaks, so the link is by analogy. Davlatjon's streak is already described as gentle (rich-phone-home-t3.jpg shows '🔥 3 дня подряд'). Check the broken-streak screen: no sad flame, no 'you lost', no push notification to rescue it, and no streak freeze that can be bought. Show 'Звёзд дня: 0' as an empty star outline, not a zero count that looks like a score of failure.
- Hidden opt-outs and navigation traps — Radesky 2022: navigation constraints and opt-out buttons less visible than purchase buttons (example: Kick the Buddy). ICO standard 13 (opened): a big 'yes' next to a small 'no', or a one-click low-privacy path versus a six-click high-privacy path, counts as a nudge. For Davlatjon: the sync prompt, the parent PIN, and 'Закончить' versus 'Ещё одну?' must have equal size and contrast. Never put a tiny grey 'нет, спасибо' next to a large orange 'да'.
- Ads, sponsored content and reward-for-watching — NN/g (opened) found children cannot distinguish ads from real content and lack the skills to identify advertising. Radesky 2022 found roadblock ads over 20 seconds (21.8% of apps), ads timed to appear when the player tries to leave (18.1%) and ads offering rewards for viewing (16.5%). Keep the product ad-free for children. Credits and links to Wikimedia Commons in the history page (image attribution) must be styled as small text links and not as buttons in the content flow.
- Forced continuity and hard-to-cancel subscriptions — From background knowledge only (the FTC press release URL I tried returned 404, so I could not read it): in 2020 the FTC settled with the children's learning service ABCmouse for $10 million over cancellation difficulties. If Davlatjon ever sells a plan, cancellation must be as easy as signup, in the parent area, and a child's screen must never show prices. Not a current issue; the product has no billing.
- Showing rating numbers, public rankings and 'you lost' counters to under-10s — This is the owner's own rule (no ratings for under 10), and it is well placed: a hidden puzzle rating drives difficulty without turning each puzzle into a verdict. Keep it hidden in the UI, in the share image and in the printable certificate. For 10+ any comparison should default to 'against my own past' and be opt-in; a public leaderboard of children also raises data questions (see COPPA pattern).
- Mystery-meat navigation: unlabeled icons and identical emoji — NN/g (opened) shows children read interface elements literally and ask what an unlabelled number means. Davlatjon has two identical 🔢 task tabs, an icon-only header, and hundreds of interactive elements with no accessible name on some pages (openings 554, games 196, endgames 54). Add labels or names so screen readers, voice control and a parent helping can use them.
- Auto-play, infinite scroll and auto-advance — ICO standard 5 (opened) lists continuous scrolling and auto-play as tactics that make it hard for children to disengage, and recommends avoiding features that extend use without an active choice. Do not auto-start the next puzzle, next narration or next day. The Woodpecker and puzzle modes should show a 'Дальше' tap and a visible stop point after a small batch (for example 5 puzzles).
- A special 'dyslexia font' as the accessibility fix — Wery and Diliberto 2017 (12 students, opened) found OpenDyslexic gave no reading gain and children did not prefer it. Spending a feature on a font switch gives false assurance. Use size, spacing, left alignment, audio and short text instead. The study is small, so say 'no evidence of benefit' and not 'proven useless'.
